sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸亥，魏以北海王顥為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、相州刺史。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on day guihai, Wei appointed the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and regional inspector of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's guihai day, Northern Wei appointed the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 魏北道行台楊津守定州城，居鮮于修禮、杜洛周之間，迭來攻圍；

translations.literal: Yang Jin, mobile-staff commander of Wei's northern circuit, held Ding province city, situated between Xianyu Xiuli and Du Luozhou; they came in turn to attack and besiege it;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jin, commander of the Northern Wei mobile staff, held Dingzhou city between the forces of Xianyu Xiuli and Du Luozhou, and the rebels attacked and besieged it in turn;

sentences.zh: 津蓄薪糧，治器械，隨機拒擊，賊不能克。

translations.literal: Jin stored firewood and grain, prepared weapons, and repelled attacks as circumstances dictated; the bandits could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jin stockpiled fuel and grain, readied arms, and struck back as opportunity allowed, and the rebels could not capture the city.

sentences.zh: 津潛使人以鐵券說賊黨，賊黨有應津者，遺津書曰：「賊所以圍城，正為取北人耳。

translations.literal: Jin secretly sent men to win over the bandit faction with iron tallies; some in the bandit faction who sided with Jin sent Jin a letter saying: "The reason the bandits besiege the city is simply to seize the northerners.
translations.idiomatic: Jin secretly sent agents to sway the rebel ranks with iron tallies of amnesty; sympathizers inside the rebel camp wrote to him: "The rebels besiege the city only to seize the northerners within.

sentences.zh: 城中北人，宜盡殺之，不然，必為患。

translations.literal: The northerners in the city should all be killed; otherwise they will surely become a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: You should kill every northerner in the city, or they will surely become a danger.

sentences.zh: 」津悉收北人內子城中而不殺，眾無不感其仁。

translations.literal: " Jin gathered all the northerners inside the inner city and did not kill them; none among the people failed to be moved by his humanity.
translations.idiomatic: " Jin brought every northerner into the inner citadel and spared them, and the whole garrison was won by his mercy.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮代修禮統眾，使人說津，許以為司徒；

translations.literal: When Ge Rong replaced Xiuli in command of the host, he sent men to persuade Jin, promising to make him Minister over the Masses;
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong succeeded Xiuli as leader of the rebels, he sent envoys to win Yang Jin over with the promise of the post of Minister over the Masses;

sentences.zh: 津斬其使，固守三年。

translations.literal: Jin beheaded the envoys and held firm for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Jin executed the envoys and held out for three years.

sentences.zh: 杜洛周圍之，魏不能救。

translations.literal: Du Luozhou besieged the city; Wei could not rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luozhou invested the city, and the Wei court could not relieve it.

sentences.zh: 津遣其子遁突圍出，詣柔然頭兵可汗求救。

translations.literal: Jin sent his son Dun to break out of the encirclement and go to beg aid from the Rouran khan Toubing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent his son Dun to break through the siege and seek help from Toubing, khan of the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 遁日夜泣請，頭兵遣其從祖吐豆發帥精騎一萬南出。

translations.literal: Dun wept and pleaded day and night; Toubing sent his father's younger cousin Tudufa to lead ten thousand elite horsemen south.
translations.idiomatic: Dun pleaded day and night in tears; Toubing dispatched his father's younger cousin Tudufa at the head of ten thousand picked horsemen to march south.

sentences.zh: 前鋒至廣昌，賊塞隘口，柔然遂還。

translations.literal: The vanguard reached Guangchang; the bandits blocked the pass, and the Rouran turned back.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard reached Guangchang, but the rebels blocked the defile and the Rouran withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，津長史李裔引賊入，執津，欲烹之，既而捨之。

translations.literal: On day yichou, Jin's chief clerk Li Yi led the bandits in, seized Jin, and was about to boil him alive, but then let him go.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Jin's chief clerk Li Yi admitted the rebels, seized Jin, and was about to boil him alive, then relented and spared him.

sentences.zh: 瀛州刺史元寧以城降洛周。

translations.literal: Yuan Ning, regional inspector of Ying province, surrendered the city to Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ning, inspector of Ying province, surrendered his city to Du Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏潘嬪生女，胡太后詐言皇子。

translations.literal: On day yichou, the Wei consort Pan gave birth to a girl; Empress Dowager Hu falsely announced a prince.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Consort Pan of Wei bore a girl, and Empress Dowager Hu falsely announced that a prince had been born.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，大赦，改元武泰。

translations.literal: On day bingyin, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Wutai.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶寅圍馮翊，未下；

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin besieged Fengyi but had not taken it;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin besieged Fengyi but had not yet captured it;

sentences.zh: 長孫稚軍至恆農，行台左丞楊侃謂稚曰：「昔魏武與韓遂、馬超據潼關相拒，遂、超之才，非魏武敵也，然而勝負久不決者，扼其險要故也。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Zhi's army reached Hengnong; Yang Kan, left director of the mobile staff, said to Zhi: "In former times Emperor Wu of Wei opposed Han Sui and Ma Chao at Tong Pass; Sui and Chao's talent was no match for Emperor Wu's, yet victory and defeat long remained undecided because he held the strategic choke point.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Zhi's army reached Hengnong; Yang Kan, left director of the mobile staff, said to Zhi: "Long ago Cao Cao held Tong Pass against Han Sui and Ma Chao. Sui and Chao were no match for him in talent, yet the struggle dragged on because he was pinned at a vital choke point.

sentences.zh: 今賊守禦已固，雖魏武復生，無以施其智勇。

translations.literal: Now the bandits' defenses are already firm; even if Emperor Wu were reborn, he could not deploy his wisdom and courage.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' defenses are already solid; even if Cao Cao himself returned, he could not bring his wit and valor to bear.

sentences.zh: 不如北取蒲阪，渡河而西，入其腹心，置兵死地，則華州之圍不戰自解，潼關之守必內顧而走。

translations.literal: Better to go north and take Puban, cross the river westward, enter their vitals, and place troops where they must fight to the death—then the siege of Hua province will lift without battle, and the Tong Pass garrison will surely turn inward and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Better march north, seize Puban, cross west of the Yellow River, and strike into their heartland with troops driven to desperation—then the siege of Huazhou will lift without a fight, and the Tong Pass garrison will turn homeward and break.

sentences.zh: 支節既解，長安可坐取也。

translations.literal: Once the branches are cut, Chang'an can be taken at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Once those limbs are severed, Chang'an can be taken at leisure.

sentences.zh: 若愚計可取，願為明公前驅。

translations.literal: If this humble plan can be adopted, I wish to serve my lord as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: If this plan suits you, I ask to lead the van for you.

sentences.zh: 」稚曰：「子之計則善矣；

translations.literal: " Zhi said: "Your plan is indeed good;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi said, "Your plan is sound;

sentences.zh: 然今薛修義圍河東，薛鳳賢據安邑，宗正珍孫守虞板不得進，如何可往？

translations.literal: but now Xue Xiuyi besieges Hedong, Xue Fengxian holds Anyi, and Zongsun Zhensun guards Yuban and cannot advance—how can we go?
translations.idiomatic: but Xue Xiuyi now besieges Hedong, Xue Fengxian holds Anyi, and Zongsun Zhensun blocks Yuban so we cannot get through—how can we march?

sentences.zh: 」侃曰：「珍孫行陳一夫，因緣為將，可為人使，安能使人！

translations.literal: " Kan said: "Zhensun is a common soldier of the ranks who rose by chance to command; he can be used by others—how can he use others!
translations.idiomatic: " Kan said, "Zhensun is a common soldier who rose by luck to command; others can use him—he cannot use others!

sentences.zh: 河東治在蒲反，西逼河漘，封疆多在郡東。

translations.literal: The seat of Hedong lies at Puban, pressed on the west by the riverbank; most of the commandery's territory lies east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong's administrative seat is at Puban, hugging the river on the west, and most of the commandery lies east of the city.

sentences.zh: 修義驅帥士民西圍郡城，其父母妻子皆留舊村，一旦聞官軍來至，皆有內顧之心，必望風自潰矣。

translations.literal: Xiuyi drives officers, soldiers, and commoners west to besiege the commandery seat; their parents, wives, and children all remain in their old villages—once they hear the government army has arrived, every man will look homeward and surely scatter at the first rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi has driven officers, troops, and townsfolk west to invest the seat, while their parents, wives, and children remain in the old hamlets—once they hear the imperial army is come, every man will look homeward and melt away at the first wind.

sentences.zh: 」稚乃使其子子彥與侃帥騎兵自恆農北渡，據石錐壁，侃聲言：「今且停此以待步兵，且觀民情向背。

translations.literal: " Zhi then sent his son Ziyan and Kan to lead cavalry north from Hengnong, seize Shizhui cliff, and Kan proclaimed: "We halt here for now to await the foot soldiers and to observe where the people's hearts lie.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi then sent his son Ziyan and Kan with cavalry to cross north from Hengnong, occupy Shizhui cliff, and Kan announced: "We pause here to await the infantry and to see which way the people lean.

sentences.zh: 命送降名者各自還村，俟台軍舉三烽，當亦舉烽相應；

translations.literal: He ordered those who submitted their names to return each to his village; when the mobile-staff army raises three beacon fires, you too shall raise beacons in answer;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered anyone who wished to surrender to return to his village; when the mobile staff lights three beacon fires, you are to light beacons in reply;

sentences.zh: 其無應烽者，乃賊黨也，當進擊屠之，以所獲賞軍。

translations.literal: those who do not answer with beacons are bandit partisans and shall be attacked and slaughtered, with the spoils given as army reward.
translations.idiomatic: any hamlet that does not answer is rebel territory and will be stormed and put to the sword, and the booty will reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 」於是村民轉相告語，雖實未降者亦詐舉烽，一宿之間，火光遍數百里。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the villagers told one another; even those who had not truly surrendered also falsely lit beacons, and within one night fires blazed across several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: " The villagers passed word among themselves; even those who had not surrendered lit false beacons, and within a single night fires stretched across hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 賊圍城者不測其故，各自散歸；

translations.literal: The bandits besieging the city could not fathom the cause and each scattered homeward;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels investing the city could not guess what had happened and drifted home in confusion;

sentences.zh: 修義亦逃還，與鳳賢俱請降。

translations.literal: Xiuyi also fled back and, with Fengxian, both asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi fled as well, and he and Fengxian both sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 丙子，稚克潼關，遂入河東。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, Zhi took Tong Pass and then entered Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Zhi captured Tong Pass and marched into Hedong.

sentences.zh: 會有詔廢鹽池稅，稚上表以為：「鹽池天產之貨，密邇京畿，唯應寶而守之，均贍以理。

translations.literal: Just then an edict abolished the salt-pond tax; Zhi submitted a memorial stating: "The salt ponds are Heaven's own produce, close to the capital region; they should be treasured and guarded, and their benefit shared by fair regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had just abolished the salt-pond levy; Zhi memorialized: "The salt ponds are a gift of nature hard by the capital; they should be guarded as treasure and their yield distributed by fair rule.

sentences.zh: 今四方多虞，府藏罄竭，冀、定擾攘，常謂之絹不復可收，唯仰府庫，有出無入。

translations.literal: Now troubles rise on every side, the treasury is empty, Ji and Ding are in turmoil, and it is commonly said that their silk tribute can never be collected again; the court can rely only on the treasury, with outflow and no inflow.
translations.idiomatic: Trouble rises on every side, the treasury stands empty, Ji and Ding are in chaos, and men say their silk tribute will never be collected again—the court lives only on the treasury, spending without replenishment.

sentences.zh: 略論鹽稅，一年之中，准絹而言，不減三十萬匹，乃是移冀、定二州置於畿甸。

translations.literal: Roughly reckoning the salt tax, in one year, measured in silk, it is no less than three hundred thousand bolts—this is like moving Ji and Ding two provinces into the capital district.
translations.idiomatic: A rough tally of the salt tax, reckoned in silk, brings no less than three hundred thousand bolts a year—equivalent to planting Ji and Ding inside the capital domain.

sentences.zh: 今若廢之，事同再失。

translations.literal: If it is abolished now, the matter is like losing twice over.
translations.idiomatic: To abolish it now would be to lose the same ground twice.

sentences.zh: 臣前仰違嚴旨，而先討關賊，逕解河東者，非緩長安而急薄阪，一失鹽池，三軍乏食。

translations.literal: Your servant earlier disobeyed the stern order and first attacked the Tong Pass bandits and went straight to relieve Hedong—not because Chang'an was slow and Puban urgent, but because once the salt ponds were lost, the three armies would lack food.
translations.idiomatic: I earlier defied your stern command and struck the Tong Pass rebels first, then relieved Hedong—not because I slighted Chang'an for Puban, but because without the salt ponds the whole army would go hungry.

sentences.zh: 天助大魏，茲計不爽。

translations.literal: Heaven aided Great Wei; this plan did not miss.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven aided Great Wei, and the plan did not fail.

sentences.zh: 昔高祖昇平之年，無所乏少，猶創置鹽官而加典護，非與物競利，恐由利而亂俗也。

translations.literal: In former times, in the years of Gaozu's peace, when nothing was lacking, he still created salt officials and added overseers—not to compete with the people for profit, but for fear that profit would disorder custom.
translations.idiomatic: Even in Gaozu's peaceful years, when the realm wanted for nothing, he still created salt officers and added overseers—not to wring profit from the people, but lest profit corrupt custom.

sentences.zh: 況今國用不足，租征六年之粟，調折來歲之資，此皆奪人私財，事不獲已。

translations.literal: How much more now, when state expenditure is insufficient, rent is levied for six years' grain, and corvée drafts next year's resources—these all seize private wealth, and the matter cannot be helped.
translations.idiomatic: How much more today, when the treasury runs short, rent is taken six years ahead, and corvée drafts next year's stores—all seizing private wealth because there is no choice.

sentences.zh: 臣輒符同監將、尉，還帥所部，依常收稅，更聽後敕。

translations.literal: Your servant has already coordinated with the supervising generals and commandants, returned to lead his command, and collected tax as usual, awaiting further orders.
translations.idiomatic: I have already coordinated with the supervising generals and commandants, returned to my command, and continued collection as before, pending further instruction.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶寅遣其將侯終德擊毛遐。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin sent his general Hou Zhongde to attack Mao Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin sent his general Hou Zhongde to attack Mao Xia.

sentences.zh: 會郭子恢等屢為魏軍所敗，終德因其勢挫，還軍襲寶寅；

translations.literal: Just then Guo Zihui and others had repeatedly been defeated by the Wei army; Zhongde, taking advantage of their shattered momentum, turned his army to strike Baoyin;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zihui and others had just suffered repeated defeats by the Wei army; Zhongde, seeing their collapse, turned his troops to strike Baoyin;

sentences.zh: 至白門，寶寅始覺，丁丑，與終德戰，敗，攜其妻南陽公主及其少子帥麾下百餘騎自後門出，奔-{万俟}-丑奴。

translations.literal: reaching White Gate, Baoyin only then realized it; on day dingchou he fought Zhongde, was defeated, and taking his wife the Princess of Nanyang and his young son led a little more than a hundred horsemen out the rear gate and fled to Moqi Chounu.
translations.idiomatic: at White Gate Baoyin learned of the revolt too late; on dingchou he fought Zhongde, lost, and with his wife the Princess of Nanyang and his young son led a little more than a hundred horsemen out the rear gate to Moqi Chounu.

sentences.zh: 丑奴以寶寅為太傅。

translations.literal: Chounu made Baoyin Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu appointed Baoyin Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 二月，魏以長孫稚為車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、雍州刺史、尚書僕射、西道行台。

translations.literal: In the second month, Wei appointed Zhangsun Zhi Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, regional inspector of Yong province, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and commander of the western-circuit mobile staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Wei appointed Zhangsun Zhi Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, inspector of Yong province, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and commander of the western mobile staff.

sentences.zh: 群盜李洪攻燒鞏西闕口以東，南結諸蠻；

translations.literal: The bandit Li Hong attacked and burned east of the western pass of Gong, and allied in the south with various Man tribes;
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Li Hong raided and burned east of Gong's western pass and allied in the south with various tribal chiefs;

sentences.zh: 魏都督李神軌、武衛將軍費穆討之。

translations.literal: the Wei commander Li Shengui and the Martial Guard general Fei Mu campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei commander Li Shengui and Martial Guard general Fei Mu marched against him.

sentences.zh: 穆敗洪於闕口南，遂平之。

translations.literal: Mu defeated Hong south of the pass and thereupon pacified the region.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu routed Li Hong south of the pass and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 葛榮擊杜洛周，殺之，並其眾。

translations.literal: Ge Rong attacked Du Luozhou, killed him, and absorbed his host.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong attacked Du Luozhou, killed him, and absorbed his forces.

sentences.zh: 魏靈太后再臨朝以來，嬖倖用事，政事縱弛，威恩不立，盜賊蜂起，封疆日蹙。

translations.literal: Since Empress Dowager Ling of Wei resumed regency, favorites held power, government grew lax, authority and favor were not established, bandits swarmed up, and the borders shrank day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Since Empress Dowager Hu resumed regency over Northern Wei, favorites had held sway, government had grown slack, authority had collapsed, rebels had risen everywhere, and the frontiers shrank daily.

sentences.zh: 魏肅宗年浸長，太后自以所為不謹，恐左右聞之於帝，凡帝所愛信者，太后輒以事去之，務為壅蔽，不使帝知外事。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong of Wei gradually grew older; the empress dowager, knowing her own conduct was not circumspect, feared those about the emperor would report it to him; whenever someone the emperor loved and trusted appeared, the empress dowager would remove him on some pretext, striving to block and screen so that the emperor would not learn of outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming was growing up; the empress dowager, knowing her own conduct had been reckless, feared the court around him would tell him; whoever won the emperor's trust she removed on some pretext, walling him off so he would not learn what passed outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍昌黎谷士恢有寵於帝，使領左右；

translations.literal: Gu Shihui of Changli, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, was favored by the emperor and was made to lead the palace guard;
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shihui of Changli, Regular Attendant, had won the emperor's favor and was placed in charge of the palace guard;

sentences.zh: 太后屢諷之，欲用為州，士恢懷寵，不願出外，太后乃誣以罪而殺之。

translations.literal: the empress dowager repeatedly hinted that she wished to appoint him to a province; Shihui, cherishing favor, was unwilling to go outside, so the empress dowager framed him on a charge and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: the empress dowager repeatedly hinted she would send him to a province; Shihui, clinging to favor, refused to leave the capital, and she framed him on a charge and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 有蜜多道人，能胡語，帝常置左右，太后使人殺之於城南，而詐懸賞購賊。

translations.literal: There was also the monk Mituo, who knew barbarian languages; the emperor often kept him at his side—the empress dowager sent men to kill him south of the city and falsely posted a reward to buy the killer.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the monk Mituo, who spoke barbarian tongues and whom the emperor kept close; the empress dowager had him killed south of the city and posted a false bounty for the assassin.

sentences.zh: 由是母子之間嫌隙日深。

translations.literal: From this the rift between mother and son grew deeper day by day.
translations.idiomatic: From this the rift between mother and son deepened daily.

sentences.zh: 是時，車騎將軍、儀同三司、並、肆、汾、廣、恆、雲六州討虜大都督爾朱榮兵勢強盛，魏朝憚之。

translations.literal: At this time Erzhu Rong, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Grand Commander for Subduing Barbarians of the six provinces Bing, Xi, Fen, Guang, Heng, and Yun, was powerful in arms, and the Wei court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Erzhu Rong—Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and grand commander for the six northern provinces Bing, Xi, Fen, Guang, Heng, and Yun—commanded a formidable army, and the Wei court stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 高歡、段榮、尉景、蔡俊先在杜洛周黨中，欲圖洛周，不果，逃奔葛榮，又亡歸爾朱榮。

translations.literal: Gao Huan, Duan Rong, Wei Jing, and Cai Jun had first been in Du Luozhou's faction, wished to plot against Luozhou but failed, fled to Ge Rong, and then fled again to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, Duan Rong, Wei Jing, and Cai Jun had first served Du Luozhou, plotted against him without success, fled to Ge Rong, and then deserted to Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 劉貴先在爾朱榮所，屢薦歡於榮，榮見其憔悴，未之奇也。

translations.literal: Liu Gui had long been with Erzhu Rong and repeatedly recommended Huan to Rong; Rong saw him haggard and did not regard him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui had long been in Erzhu Rong's service and repeatedly praised Gao Huan to him; Rong saw how gaunt he was and thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 歡從榮之馬廄，廄有悍馬，榮命歡剪之，歡不加羈絆而剪之，竟不蹄嚙；

translations.literal: Huan followed Rong to the stables; there was a fierce horse in the stable, and Rong ordered Huan to groom it; Huan groomed it without putting on hobbles, and in the end it did not kick or bite;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan followed Rong to the stables, where a vicious horse was kept; Rong ordered him to groom it; Huan worked without hobbling the beast, and it never kicked or bit;

sentences.zh: 起，謂榮曰：「御惡人亦猶是矣。

translations.literal: rising, he said to Rong: "Taming wicked men is just the same.
translations.idiomatic: then he rose and said to Rong, "Controlling wicked men is the same.

sentences.zh: 」榮奇其言，坐歡於床下，屏左右，訪以時事。

translations.literal: " Rong marveled at his words, seated Huan below his couch, dismissed those about him, and questioned him on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong was struck by the remark, seated Huan at the foot of his couch, dismissed his attendants, and questioned him on the times.

sentences.zh: 歡曰：「聞公有馬十二谷，色別為群，畜此竟何用也？

translations.literal: Huan said: "I hear that my lord has horses in twelve valleys, sorted by color into herds—what use is raising them?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "I hear you keep horses in twelve valleys, sorted by color into herds—what are you saving them for?

sentences.zh: 」榮曰：「但言爾意！

translations.literal: " Rong said: "Just speak your mind!
translations.idiomatic: " Rong said, "Speak your mind!

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「今天子闇弱，太后淫亂，嬖孽擅命，朝政不行。

translations.literal: " Huan said: "Today the Son of Heaven is dim and weak, the empress dowager is dissolute, favorites usurp command, and court government does not go forward.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan said, "The Son of Heaven is weak, the empress dowager debauched, favorites usurp authority, and the court cannot govern.

sentences.zh: 以明公雄武，乘時奮發，討鄭儼、徐紇之罪以清帝側，霸業可舉鞭而成，此賀六渾之意也。

translations.literal: With my lord's heroic might, if you seize the moment and strike, punish Zheng Yan and Xu He to cleanse the emperor's side, hegemony can be achieved with a flick of the whip—this is Helejin's thought.
translations.idiomatic: With your valor, if you seize the moment, punish Zheng Yan and Xu He to purge the emperor's household, empire can be won with a flick of the whip—that is Helejin's counsel.

sentences.zh: 」榮大悅。

translations.literal: " Rong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 語自日中至夜半乃出，自是每參軍謀。

translations.literal: They talked from midday until midnight before he left; from then on he joined in every military plan.
translations.idiomatic: They talked from noon until midnight before Huan left; thereafter he took part in every military deliberation.

sentences.zh: 并州刺史元天穆，孤之五世孫也，與榮善，榮兄事之。

translations.literal: Yuan Tianmu, regional inspector of Bing province, was a fifth-generation descendant of the imperial house; he was on good terms with Rong, and Rong treated him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tianmu, inspector of Bing province, was a fifth-generation descendant of the imperial clan; he was close to Erzhu Rong, who treated him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 榮常與天穆及帳下都督賀拔岳密謀，欲舉兵入洛，內誅嬖倖，外清群盜，二人皆勸成之。

translations.literal: Rong often plotted secretly with Tianmu and his camp commander Heba Yue to raise troops and enter Luoyang, execute the favorites within and clear away the bandits without; both men urged him to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Rong often plotted in secret with Tianmu and his camp commander Heba Yue to march on Luoyang, kill the favorites within and pacify the rebels without; both urged him to act.

sentences.zh: 榮上書，以「山東群盜方熾，冀、定覆沒，官軍屢敗，請遣精騎三千東援相州。

translations.literal: Rong submitted a memorial stating: "Bandits east of the mountains are still raging; Ji and Ding are overrun, and the government army has repeatedly been defeated—please send three thousand elite horsemen east to aid Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong memorialized: "Rebels east of the mountains still rage; Ji and Ding have fallen, and the imperial army has been beaten again and again—send three thousand elite horsemen east to relieve Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 」太后疑之，報以「念生梟戮，寶寅就擒，丑奴請降，關、隴已定。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager was suspicious and replied: "Niannian has been beheaded, Baoyin has been captured, Chounu has asked to surrender, and Guanlong is already settled.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager was suspicious and answered: "Moqi Niannian has been executed, Baoyin taken, Chounu has sued for surrender, and Guanlong is pacified.

sentences.zh: 費穆大破群蠻，絳蜀漸平。

translations.literal: Fei Mu has greatly defeated the tribal rebels, and the Jiang and Shu disturbances are gradually being pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu has crushed the tribal rebels, and trouble in Jiang and Shu is easing.

sentences.zh: 又，北海王顥帥眾二萬出鎮相州，不須出兵。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, leads twenty thousand men out to garrison Xiang province; there is no need to send troops.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, leads twenty thousand men to garrison Xiang province—no expedition is needed.

sentences.zh: 」榮復上書，以為：「賊勢雖衰，官軍屢敗，人情危怯，恐實難用。

translations.literal: " Rong submitted another memorial, stating: "Though the bandits' momentum has waned, the government army has repeatedly been defeated; men's hearts are fearful and timid, and I fear they truly cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong memorialized again: "Though rebel strength has faded, the imperial army keeps losing; hearts are timid, and I fear the troops cannot be relied on.

sentences.zh: 若不更思方略，無以萬全。

translations.literal: If we do not rethink our strategy, there is no way to be wholly secure.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we rethink our strategy, there is no sure safety.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為蠕蠕主阿那瑰荷國厚恩，未應忘報，宜遣發兵東趣下口以躡其背，北海之事嚴加警備以當其前。

translations.literal: Your servant is of the humble opinion that the Rouran ruler Anagui has received the state's great grace and ought not forget repayment; he should be ordered to send troops east toward Xiakou to tread on the enemy's rear, while the Beihai affair should be strictly guarded in front.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the Rouran khan Anagui owes the state a great debt and should not forget it—he should be ordered east toward Xiakou to strike the enemy's rear, while the Beihai front is held in strict readiness.

sentences.zh: 臣麾下雖少，輒盡力命。

translations.literal: Though few are under your servant's command, I will exhaust my strength to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Few as my own troops are, I will spend them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 自井陘以北，滏口以西，分據險要，攻其肘腋。

translations.literal: From north of Jingxing to west of Fukou, we shall divide and hold the strategic points and strike their flanks.
translations.idiomatic: From north of Jingxing to west of Fukou we shall seize the passes and strike their flanks.

sentences.zh: 葛榮雖並洛周，威恩未著，人類差異，形勢可分。

translations.literal: Though Ge Rong has absorbed Luozhou, his authority and favor are not yet established; men differ in kind, and the situation can be divided.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ge Rong has absorbed Luozhou's host, his authority is not yet secure; the rebels are not one body, and their force can be split.

sentences.zh: 」遂勒兵，召集義勇，北捍馬邑，東塞井陘。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he marshaled troops, summoned volunteers, defended Mayi in the north, and blocked Jingxing in the east.
translations.idiomatic: " He then mobilized his army, called up volunteers, held Mayi in the north, and sealed Jingxing in the east.

sentences.zh: 徐紇說太后以鐵券間榮左右，榮聞而恨之。

translations.literal: Xu He persuaded the empress dowager to use iron tallies to win over men about Rong; Rong heard of it and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He persuaded the empress dowager to suborn Erzhu Rong's officers with iron tallies of amnesty; Rong learned of it and came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 魏肅宗亦惡儼、紇等，逼於太后，不能去。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong of Wei also hated Yan, He, and the rest, but pressed by the empress dowager he could not remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming likewise hated Zheng Yan, Xu He, and their faction, but bound by the empress dowager he could not remove them.

sentences.zh: 密詔榮舉兵內向，欲以脅太后。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered Rong to raise troops and march inward, intending to coerce the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered Erzhu Rong to march on the capital, intending to intimidate the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 榮以高歡為前鋒，行至上黨，帝復以私詔止之。

translations.literal: Rong made Gao Huan his vanguard; when they reached Shangdang the emperor again sent a private order halting them.
translations.idiomatic: Rong made Gao Huan his vanguard; when the army reached Shangdang the emperor sent another private order to halt the march.

sentences.zh: 儼、紇恐禍及己，陰與太后謀鴆帝。

translations.literal: Yan and He, fearing disaster would reach themselves, plotted secretly with the empress dowager to poison the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and He, fearing ruin for themselves, plotted secretly with the empress dowager to poison the emperor.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，帝暴殂。

translations.literal: On day guichou the emperor died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou the emperor died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，太后立皇女為帝，大赦。

translations.literal: On day jiayin the empress dowager enthroned the imperial daughter as emperor and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the empress dowager enthroned the infant princess as emperor and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 既而下詔稱：「潘充華本實生女，故臨洮王寶暉世子釗，體自高祖，宜膺大寶。

translations.literal: Then she issued an edict stating: "Consort Pan had in truth borne a girl; therefore the heir Yuan Zhao of Prince Bao of Lintao, his person deriving from Gaozu, should receive the great mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Then she issued an edict: "Consort Pan had in truth borne a girl; therefore Yuan Zhao, heir of Prince Bao of Lintao, descended from Gaozu, should receive the great mandate.

sentences.zh: 百官文武加二階，宿衛加三階。

translations.literal: All civil and military officials were promoted two ranks; palace guards three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: All civil and military officials were promoted two ranks, palace guards three ranks.

sentences.zh: 」乙卯，釗即位。

translations.literal: " On day yimao Zhao took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " On yimao Zhao ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 釗始生三歲，太后欲久專政，故貪其幼而立之。

translations.literal: Zhao had only just been born three years; the empress dowager wished to hold power for long, so she coveted his youth and enthroned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was only three years old; the empress dowager wished to keep power for herself, and so she set him on the throne because he was still a child.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮聞之，大怒，謂元天穆曰：「主上晏駕，春秋十九，海內猶謂之幼君；

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong heard of it, was greatly angered, and said to Yuan Tianmu: "The late sovereign has passed away at nineteen; within the seas men still call him a young ruler;
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong heard of this he was furious. He said to Yuan Tianmu, "Our late lord died at nineteen, and the realm still called him a young emperor;

sentences.zh: 況今奉未言之兒以臨天下，欲求治安，其可得乎！

translations.literal: how much less now, when an infant who cannot yet speak is set to rule all under Heaven—can order and peace be sought?
translations.idiomatic: how can we expect peace when an infant who cannot yet speak is set to rule the empire?

sentences.zh: 吾欲帥鐵騎赴哀山陵，剪除奸佞，更立長君，何如？

translations.literal: I wish to lead iron cavalry to mourn at the mountain tomb, cut down traitors and flatterers, and set up a mature ruler—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to lead my armored horsemen to the imperial tombs in mourning, purge the traitors, and enthrone a grown prince. What say you?

sentences.zh: 」天穆曰：「此伊、霍復見於今矣！

translations.literal: " Tianmu said: "This is Yi Yin and Huo Guang seen again in our day!
translations.idiomatic: " Tianmu said, "This is Yi Yin and Huo Guang reborn in our age!

sentences.zh: 」乃抗表稱：「大行皇帝背棄萬方，海內咸稱鴆毒致禍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he submitted a defiant memorial stating: "The late emperor has abandoned the myriad regions; within the seas all say he met calamity through poison.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted a defiant memorial: "The late emperor has abandoned the realm, and all under Heaven say he was poisoned.

sentences.zh: 豈有天子不豫，初不召醫，貴戚大臣皆不侍側，安得不使遠近怪愕！

translations.literal: When a Son of Heaven falls ill, is there ever a case where physicians are not summoned at first, and noble kin and great ministers do not attend his side—how could this fail to startle near and far!
translations.idiomatic: When an emperor falls ill, physicians are summoned and kin and ministers attend him—how could the court do neither without shocking the realm?

sentences.zh: 又以皇女為儲兩，虛行赦宥。

translations.literal: Again they took an imperial daughter for the heir apparent and falsely proclaimed an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: They passed off an imperial daughter as the heir and proclaimed a hollow amnesty.

sentences.zh: 上欺天地，下惑朝野。

translations.literal: Above they deceive Heaven and Earth; below they delude court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: They deceive Heaven and Earth above and delude court and countryside below.

sentences.zh: 已乃選君於孩提之中，實使奸豎專朝，隳亂綱紀，此何異掩目捕雀，塞耳盜鐘！

translations.literal: Then they chose a ruler from among suckling children, in truth letting wicked eunuchs monopolize the court, overthrowing law and order—what difference is this from covering the eyes to catch sparrows or stopping the ears to steal a bell!
translations.idiomatic: Then they chose a ruler still in swaddling clothes and let wicked eunuchs run the court, shattering all order—as if one could catch sparrows with covered eyes or steal a bell with stopped ears!

sentences.zh: 今群盜沸騰，鄰敵窺窬，而欲以未言之兒鎮安天下，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Now bandits boil on every side and neighboring foes peer in greedily, yet they wish to calm all under Heaven with an infant who cannot yet speak—is it not hard!
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rise on every side and enemies watch from the borders, yet they would pacify the empire with a babe who cannot speak—is that not folly?

sentences.zh: 願聽臣赴闕，參預大議，問侍臣帝崩之由，訪禁衛不知之狀，以徐、鄭之徒付之司敗，雪同天之恥，謝遠近之怨，然後更擇宗親以承寶祚。

translations.literal: I beg that I be permitted to go to the capital, take part in the great deliberation, question the attendants on the cause of the emperor's death, inquire of the palace guard into what they did not know, hand over Xu, Zheng, and their kind to the judicial officer, wipe away the shame equal to Heaven, answer the resentment of near and far, and only then choose again among the imperial clan to receive the sacred succession.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to march on the capital, join the great council, demand of the attendants how the emperor died, question the guards as to what they knew, deliver Xu He, Zheng Yan, and their faction to justice, wipe away this shame before Heaven, appease the wrath of the realm, and only then choose another prince of the blood to receive the throne.

sentences.zh: 」榮從弟世隆，時為直閣，太后遣詣晉陽慰諭榮；

translations.literal: " Rong's younger cousin Shilong, then serving as Direct Attendant, was sent by the empress dowager to Jinyang to console and instruct Rong;
translations.idiomatic: " Rong's cousin Erzhu Shilong, then a Direct Attendant, was sent by the empress dowager to Jinyang to reassure him;

sentences.zh: 榮欲留之，世隆曰：「朝廷疑兄，故遣世隆來，今留世隆，使朝廷得預為之備，非計也。

translations.literal: Rong wished to detain him. Shilong said: "The court suspects my elder brother, and therefore sent Shilong; if Shilong is now detained, the court can prepare in advance—that is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wished to keep him. Shilong said, "The court mistrusts you and sent me; if you detain me, the court will have time to prepare—that is no strategy.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣之。

translations.literal: " He then sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: " He let him go.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸未，葛榮陷魏滄州，執刺史薛慶之，居民死者什八九。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day guiwei, Ge Rong took Wei's Cangzhou, seized regional inspector Xue Qingzhi, and of the inhabitants eight or nine in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guiwei, Ge Rong captured Cangzhou in Wei, seized Inspector Xue Qingzhi, and eight or nine tenths of the inhabitants perished.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，魏葬孝明皇帝於定陵，廟號肅宗。

translations.literal: On day yiyou, Wei buried Emperor Xiaoming at Dingling; his temple name was Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Wei buried Emperor Xiaoming at Dingling with the temple name Suzong.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮與元天穆議，以彭城武宣王有忠勳，其子長樂王子攸，素有令望，欲立之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong and Yuan Tianmu deliberated: the Martial Prince of Pengcheng had rendered loyal service, and his son, the Prince of Changle, Yuan You, had long enjoyed a fine reputation—they wished to enthrone him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong and Yuan Tianmu agreed that the Martial Prince of Pengcheng had served the dynasty faithfully and that his son Yuan You, Prince of Changle, enjoyed wide esteem—they resolved to enthrone him.

sentences.zh: 又遣從子天光及親信奚毅、倉頭王相入洛，與爾朱世隆密議。

translations.literal: They also sent Rong's nephew Tianguang and trusted men Xi Yi and the steward Wang Xiang into Luoyang to confer secretly with Erzhu Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent Rong's nephew Erzhu Tianguang and trusted agents Xi Yi and the steward Wang Xiang to Luoyang for secret talks with Erzhu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 天光見子攸，具論榮心，子攸許之。

translations.literal: Tianguang saw Prince You and fully set forth Rong's intent; Prince You consented.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang met Prince You, laid out Rong's design in full, and the prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 天光等還晉陽，榮猶疑之，乃以銅為顯祖諸子孫各鑄像，唯長樂王像成。

translations.literal: When Tianguang and the others returned to Jinyang, Rong still hesitated; he had bronze cast into images for each of the sons and grandsons of the Founding Emperor, and only the image of the Prince of Changle was completed.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang returned to Jinyang, Rong still wavered; he had bronze images cast for each descendant of the founding house, and only Prince You's image succeeded.

sentences.zh: 榮乃起兵發晉陽，世隆逃出，會榮於上黨。

translations.literal: Rong then raised his army and set out from Jinyang; Shilong fled out to join Rong at Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then marched from Jinyang; Shilong slipped out of the capital and joined him at Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 靈太后聞之，甚懼，悉召王公等入議，宗室大臣皆疾太后所為，莫肯致言。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling heard of it and was greatly afraid; she summoned princes and dukes and others into council, but the imperial kin and great ministers all resented what the empress dowager had done and none would speak.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu heard and was terrified; she summoned the princes and nobles to council, but the clan and great ministers, loathing her conduct, would not speak.

sentences.zh: 徐紇獨曰：「爾朱榮小胡，敢稱兵向闕，文武宿衛足以制之。

translations.literal: Xu He alone said: "Erzhu Rong is a petty barbarian who dares raise troops against the capital; the civil and military guards of long standing are enough to subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xu He said, "Erzhu Rong is a petty barbarian who dares march on the capital; the veteran guards of court and camp are enough to crush him.

sentences.zh: 但守險要以逸待勞，彼懸軍千里，士馬疲弊，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Only hold the strategic passes and await the weary with ease; his army hangs a thousand li away, men and horses are worn and spent—he is sure to be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the strategic passes and meet his exhausted force with rested troops; his army has marched a thousand li, men and horses are spent—he must be broken.

sentences.zh: 」太后以為然，以黃門侍郎李神軌為大都督，帥眾拒之，別將鄭季明、鄭先護將兵守河橋，武衛將軍費穆屯小平津。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager thought it right and appointed Palace Attendant Li Shengui Grand Commander to lead the host against him; separate generals Zheng Jiming and Zheng Xianhu led troops to guard Heqiao, and Martial Guard general Fei Mu encamped at Xiaoping Ford.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager agreed, appointed Palace Attendant Li Shengui grand commander to resist him, detached Zheng Jiming and Zheng Xianhu to hold Heqiao, and posted Martial Guard general Fei Mu at Xiaoping Ford.

sentences.zh: 先護，儼之從祖兄弟也。

translations.literal: Xianhu was a cousin of Zheng Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhu was a cousin of Zheng Yan.

sentences.zh: 榮至河內，復遣王相密至洛，迎長樂王子攸。

translations.literal: When Rong reached Henei, he again sent Wang Xiang secretly to Luoyang to bring out the Prince of Changle, Yuan You.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong reached Henei he again sent Wang Xiang secretly to Luoyang to bring out Prince You of Changle.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙申，子攸與兄彭城王劭、弟霸城公子正潛自高渚渡河，丁酉，會榮於河陽，將士咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on day bingshen, Prince You, his elder brother the Prince of Pengcheng, Shao, and his younger brother the Prince of Bacheng, Zizheng, secretly crossed the river from Gaozhu; on day dingyou they met Rong at Heyang, and officers and soldiers all shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingshen, Prince You with his elder brother Shao, Prince of Pengcheng, and his younger brother Zizheng, Prince of Bacheng, stole across the river from Gaozhu; on dingyou they met Rong at Heyang, and the host shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，濟河，子攸即帝位，以勳為無上王，子正為始平王；

translations.literal: On day wuxu they crossed the river; Prince You took the imperial seat and made Shao Prince of Supreme Honor and Zizheng Prince of Beginning Peace;
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu they crossed the river; Prince You took the throne, made Shao Prince of Supreme Honor, and Zizheng Prince of Beginning Peace;

sentences.zh: 以榮為侍中、都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、尚書令、領軍將軍、領左右，封太原王。

translations.literal: he made Rong Palace Attendant, Commander of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand General, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Army Supervisor, and Commander of the Left and Right, enfeoffing him as Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed Rong Palace Attendant, commander of all military affairs within and without, Grand General, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, army supervisor, and commander of the left and right guards, enfeoffing him as Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 鄭先護素與敬宗善，聞帝即位，與鄭季明開城納之。

translations.literal: Zheng Xianhu had long been on good terms with Jingzong; hearing that the emperor had taken the throne, he and Zheng Jiming opened the city and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xianhu had long been close to Yuan You; when he heard the new emperor had been enthroned, he and Zheng Jiming opened the city gates.

sentences.zh: 李神軌至河橋，聞北中不守，即遁還；

translations.literal: Li Shengui reached Heqiao, heard that the northern center was lost, and at once fled back;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shengui reached Heqiao, learned the northern crossing was lost, and fled;

sentences.zh: 費穆棄眾先降於榮。

translations.literal: Fei Mu abandoned his host and was first to surrender to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu deserted his troops and was the first to surrender to Rong.

sentences.zh: 徐紇矯詔夜開殿門，取驊騮廄御馬十匹，東奔兗州，鄭儼亦走還鄉里。

translations.literal: Xu He forged an edict to open the palace gates by night, took ten horses from the Hualiang stable, and fled east to Yanzhou; Zheng Yan also fled home to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He forged an edict, opened the palace gates by night, took ten horses from the imperial stud, and fled east to Yanzhou; Zheng Yan fled to his home district.

sentences.zh: 太后盡召肅宗後宮，皆令出家，太后亦自落髮。

translations.literal: The empress dowager summoned all the late Suzong's palace women and ordered them to take the tonsure; she too shaved her head.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned every woman of Xiaoming's harem and ordered them into religion; she shaved her own head as well.

sentences.zh: 榮召百官迎車駕，己亥，百官奉璽綬，備法駕，迎敬宗於河橋。

translations.literal: Rong summoned the hundred officials to welcome the imperial carriage; on day jihai the hundred officials presented the seal and cord, prepared the full imperial equipage, and welcomed Jingzong at Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Rong called the officials to welcome the emperor; on jihai they presented the seal and cord with full imperial pomp and received Emperor Xiaozhuang at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 庚子，榮遣騎執太后及幼主，送至河陰。

translations.literal: On day gengzi, Rong sent horsemen to seize the empress dowager and the young sovereign and convey them to Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Rong sent horsemen to seize the empress dowager and the child emperor and take them to Heyin.

sentences.zh: 太后對榮多所陳說，榮拂衣而起，沉太后及幼主於河。

translations.literal: The empress dowager made many pleas to Rong; Rong brushed his robe and rose, and drowned the empress dowager and the young sovereign in the river.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager pleaded at length; Rong brushed his robe aside, rose, and had her and the child emperor drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 費穆密說榮曰：「公士馬不出萬人，今長驅向洛，前無橫陳，既無戰勝之威，群情素不厭服。

translations.literal: Fei Mu secretly said to Rong: "Your lordship's men and horses do not exceed ten thousand; now you drive straight to Luoyang with no barrier before you—there is neither the prestige of victory, nor has popular feeling long submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu whispered to Rong, "You have fewer than ten thousand men and have marched straight on Luoyang without a battle won; you lack the awe of victory, and the realm has never accepted you.

sentences.zh: 以京師之眾，百官之盛，知公虛實，有輕侮之心。

translations.literal: With the multitudes of the capital and the splendor of the hundred officials, men know your lordship's emptiness and fullness and hold a heart of contempt.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is crowded, the bureaucracy vast—they know your strength and despise you.

sentences.zh: 若不大行誅罰，更樹親黨，恐公還北之日，未度太行而內變作矣。

translations.literal: If you do not carry out great executions and establish a new faction of kin, I fear that on the day you return north, before you have crossed the Taihang, internal revolt will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Unless you strike down many and build a new faction of your own, I fear that before you cross the Taihang on your way north, revolt will break out behind you.

sentences.zh: 」榮心然之，謂所親慕容紹宗曰：「洛中人士繁盛，驕侈成俗，不加芟剪，終難制馭。

translations.literal: " Rong's heart agreed; he said to his intimate Murong Shaozong: "The people of Luoyang are numerous, proud and extravagant by custom; if they are not cut down, in the end they will be hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong agreed and said to his confidant Murong Shaozong, "Luoyang is crowded with proud, extravagant men; unless they are cut down, you will never control them.

sentences.zh: 吾欲因百官出迎，悉誅之，何如？

translations.literal: I wish, when the hundred officials come out to welcome us, to kill them all—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to kill them all when they come out to welcome us—what say you?

sentences.zh: 」紹宗曰：「太后荒淫失道，嬖倖弄權，淆亂四海，故明公興義兵以清朝廷。

translations.literal: " Shaozong said: "The empress dowager was debauched and lost the Way, favorites wielded power, and the four seas were thrown into confusion—therefore your lordship raised righteous troops to cleanse the court.
translations.idiomatic: " Shaozong said, "The empress dowager debauched herself and lost the Way; favorites seized power and threw the realm into chaos—that is why you raised righteous arms to cleanse the court.

sentences.zh: 今無故殲夷多士，不分忠佞，恐大失天下之望，非長策也。

translations.literal: Now to slaughter many scholars for no reason, not distinguishing loyal from traitorous, I fear you will greatly lose the hope of all under Heaven—it is no long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: To slaughter the bureaucracy without distinguishing loyal from traitor will cost you the hope of the realm—that is no lasting policy.

sentences.zh: 」榮不聽，乃請帝循河西至淘渚，引百官於行宮西北，雲欲祭天。

translations.literal: " Rong would not listen; he asked the emperor to follow the river west to Taozhu, drew the hundred officials to the northwest of the traveling palace, and said he wished to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong would not listen. He asked the emperor to follow the river west to Taozhu, gathered the officials northwest of the traveling palace, and said he would sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 百官既集，列胡騎圍之，責以天下喪亂，肅宗暴崩，皆由朝臣貪虐，不能匡弼。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials had assembled, he arrayed barbarian horsemen about them, charged them with the realm's disorder and Suzong's violent death, all because the courtiers were greedy and cruel and could not support and correct the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials had gathered, he surrounded them with barbarian horsemen, accused them of bringing the realm to ruin and of Xiaoming's violent death through their greed and cruelty and failure to support the throne.

sentences.zh: 因縱兵殺之，自丞相高陽王雍、司空元欽、儀同三司義陽王略以下，死者二千餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he loosed his soldiers to kill them; from Chancellor Gao Yang, Prince of Gaoyang, Wang Yong, Minister of Works Yuan Qin, and Director of the Three Offices with Equal Standing, Prince of Yiyang, Wang Lue, downward, more than two thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he loosed his troops upon them. From Chancellor Wang Yong, Prince of Gaoyang, Minister of Works Yuan Qin, and Director of the Three Offices with Equal Standing Wang Lue, Prince of Yiyang, downward, more than two thousand perished.

sentences.zh: 前黃門郎王遵業兄弟居父喪，其母，敬宗之從母也，相帥出迎，俱死。

translations.literal: Former Palace Attendant Wang Zunye and his brothers were in mourning for their father; their mother was a cousin of Jingzong's mother, and they led one another out to welcome him—all died.
translations.idiomatic: Former Palace Attendant Wang Zunye and his brothers were in mourning for their father; their mother was a cousin of the emperor's mother, and they went out together to welcome him—all were killed.

sentences.zh: 遵業，慧龍之孫也，俊爽涉學，時人惜其才而譏其躁。

translations.literal: Zunye was the grandson of Wang Huilong, handsome and quick, versed in learning; men of the time mourned his talent and mocked his rashness.
translations.idiomatic: Zunye was the grandson of Wang Huilong, handsome, quick-witted, and learned; contemporaries mourned his talent and blamed his rashness.

sentences.zh: 有朝士百餘人後至，榮復以胡騎圍之，令曰：「有能為禪文者免死。

translations.literal: More than a hundred courtiers who arrived later were again surrounded by barbarian horsemen; he ordered: "Whoever can compose a text of abdication shall be spared death.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred officials who came later were again surrounded; he proclaimed, "Whoever can draft an abdication edict shall live.

sentences.zh: 」侍御史趙元則出應募，遂使為之。

translations.literal: " Attendant Censor Zhao Yuanze stepped forward to answer the call, and Rong had him compose it.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendant Censor Zhao Yuanze came forward, and Rong made him write it.

sentences.zh: 榮又令其軍士言：「元氏既滅，爾朱氏興。

translations.literal: Rong also ordered his soldiers to say: "The Yuan clan is destroyed; the Erzhu clan rises.
translations.idiomatic: Rong also ordered his soldiers to cry, "The house of Yuan is ended; the house of Erzhu rises.

sentences.zh: 」皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: " All shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: " All shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 榮又遣數十人拔刀向行宮，帝與無上王劭、始平王子正俱出帳外。

translations.literal: Rong also sent several tens of men with drawn swords toward the traveling palace; the emperor, together with the Prince of Supreme Honor, Shao, and the Prince of Beginning Peace, Zizheng, all came out of the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Rong also sent several dozen men with drawn swords toward the traveling palace; the emperor with Shao, Prince of Supreme Honor, and Zizheng, Prince of Beginning Peace, all came out of the tent.

sentences.zh: 榮先遣并州人郭羅剎、西部高車叱列殺鬼侍帝側，詐言防衛，抱帝入帳，餘人即殺劭及子正，又遣數十人遷帝於河橋，置之幕下。

translations.literal: Rong had first sent the Bingzhou man Guo Luosha and the western Gaoche Chilie to kill the ghost beside the emperor, falsely saying they were guarding him; they embraced the emperor and entered the tent, and the others at once killed Shao and Zizheng; he also sent several tens of men to move the emperor to Heqiao and place him beneath a tent.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had already sent the Bingzhou man Guo Luosha and the western Gaoche Chilie to kill the emperor's attendants on the pretext of guarding him; they seized the emperor and pulled him into the tent while the others killed Shao and Zizheng; then he sent more men to move the emperor to Heqiao and confine him under a tent.

sentences.zh: 帝憂憤無計，使人諭旨於榮曰：「帝王迭興，盛衰無常。

translations.literal: The emperor, worried and resentful, had no plan; he sent a man to convey his intent to Rong, saying: "Emperors rise in turn; prosperity and decline have no constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, desperate and without counsel, sent word to Rong: "Dynasties rise and fall; fortune has no fixed course.

sentences.zh: 今四方瓦解，將軍奮袂而起，所向無前，此乃天意，非人力也。

translations.literal: Now the four quarters are shattered; the general has raised his sleeve and risen—wherever you turn there is no one before you. This is Heaven's intent, not human power.
translations.idiomatic: The realm lies in ruins and you have risen with unstoppable force—this is Heaven's will, not man's.

sentences.zh: 我本相投，志在全生，豈敢妄希天位！

translations.literal: I at first cast myself on you, my aim being to preserve my life entirely—how would I dare vainly hope for Heaven's throne!
translations.idiomatic: I came to you only to save my life; I never dared dream of the throne!

sentences.zh: 將軍見逼，以至於此。

translations.literal: The general pressed me, and it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: You forced me to this pass.

sentences.zh: 若天命有歸，將軍宜時正尊號；

translations.literal: If Heaven's mandate has a destination, the general should at once set up the honored title;
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven has chosen you, take the throne at once;

sentences.zh: 若推而不居，存魏社稷，亦當更擇親賢而輔之。

translations.literal: if you push it away and will not occupy it, to preserve Wei's altars of state, you should also choose again among the worthy of the kin to support them.
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse it and would preserve Wei's altars, choose another worthy prince of the blood to rule.

sentences.zh: 」時都督高歡勸榮稱帝，左右多同之，榮疑未決。

translations.literal: " At that time the commander Gao Huan urged Rong to declare himself emperor; those about him mostly agreed, but Rong hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Commander Gao Huan urged Rong to take the throne; most of his followers agreed, but Rong hesitated.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳進曰：「將軍首舉義兵，志除奸逆，大勳未立，遽有此謀，正可速禍，未見其福。

translations.literal: Heba Yue advanced and said: "The general first raised righteous troops, your aim to remove traitors and the wicked; the great achievement is not yet established, and suddenly there is this design—you will quickly meet calamity, and I do not see the blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue stepped forward and said, "You raised righteous arms to purge traitors; your great work is not yet done. To plot the throne now will bring swift disaster, not fortune.

sentences.zh: 」榮乃自鑄金為像，凡四鑄，不成。

translations.literal: " Rong then cast gold into an image himself; in all he cast four times, and none succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong then cast a golden image of himself four times, and each time it failed.

sentences.zh: 功曹參軍燕郡劉靈助善卜筮，榮信之，靈助言天時人事未可。

translations.literal: Staff Officer Liu Lingzhu of Yan commandery was skilled in divination; Rong trusted him, and Lingzhu said the seasons of Heaven and affairs of men were not yet permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer Liu Lingzhu of Yan commandery was skilled in divination; Rong trusted him, and Lingzhu said Heaven and the times were not yet ripe.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「若我不吉，當迎天穆立之。

translations.literal: Rong said: "If I am unlucky, I should welcome Tianmu and enthrone him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "If the omen is against me, I should enthrone Tianmu instead.

sentences.zh: 」靈助曰：「天穆亦不吉，唯長樂王有天命耳。

translations.literal: " Lingzhu said: "Tianmu too is unlucky; only the Prince of Changle has Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: " Lingzhu said, "Tianmu is unlucky as well; only the Prince of Changle bears Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 」榮亦精神恍惚，不自支持。

translations.literal: " Rong's spirit was also confused and dazed; he could not support himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong's mind grew clouded; he could scarcely stand.

sentences.zh: 久而方寤，深自愧悔曰：「過誤若是，唯當以死謝朝廷。

translations.literal: After a long while he came to himself and, deeply ashamed and repentant, said: "A fault like this can only be answered with death before the court.
translations.idiomatic: At length he came to himself and said in deep shame, "A crime like this can only be expiated with my life before the throne.

sentences.zh: 」賀拔岳請殺高歡以謝天下，左右皆曰：「歡雖復愚疏，言不思難，今四方多事，須藉武將，請捨之，收其後效。

translations.literal: " Heba Yue asked to kill Gao Huan to answer all under Heaven; those about him all said: "Though Huan is foolish and crude and his words do not consider difficulty, now the four quarters have many affairs and we must rely on martial generals—please spare him and await his later service.
translations.idiomatic: " Heba Yue asked to execute Gao Huan to appease the realm; his attendants said, "Gao Huan is rash and his words reckless, but the realm is still in turmoil and we need fighting men—spare him and wait for his service.

sentences.zh: 」榮乃止。

translations.literal: " Rong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong desisted.

sentences.zh: 夜四更，復迎帝還榮，榮望馬首叩頭請死。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch of the night he again welcomed the emperor back to Rong's camp; Rong looked to the horse's head, knocked his head, and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch he brought the emperor back to camp; Rong bowed to the ground before his horse and begged to die.

sentences.zh: 榮所從胡騎殺朝士既多，不敢入洛城，即欲向北為遷都之計。

translations.literal: The barbarian horsemen who followed Rong had killed so many courtiers that they dared not enter Luoyang city; they wished at once to go north and plan to move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's barbarian horsemen had slaughtered so many officials that they dared not enter Luoyang and wished to march north and move the capital.

sentences.zh: 榮狐疑甚久，武衛將軍汎禮固諫。

translations.literal: Rong hesitated for a very long time; Martial Guard general Fan Li firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wavered for a long time until Martial Guard general Fan Li remonstrated firmly.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，榮奉帝入城。

translations.literal: On day xinchou, Rong led the emperor into the city.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Rong escorted the emperor into the city.

sentences.zh: 帝御太極殿，下詔大赦，改元建義。

translations.literal: The emperor took his seat in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, issued an edict of great amnesty, and changed the era name to Jianyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the throne in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Jianyi.

sentences.zh: 從太原王將士，普加五階，在京文官二階，武官三階，百姓復租役三年。

translations.literal: The soldiers who had followed the Prince of Taiyuan were all promoted five ranks; civil officials in the capital two ranks, military three ranks; the common people were exempted from rent and corvée for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who had followed the Prince of Taiyuan were promoted five ranks; civil officials in the capital two ranks, military three; commoners were exempted from rent and corvée for three years.

sentences.zh: 時百官蕩盡，存者皆竄匿不出，唯散騎常侍山偉一人拜赦於闕下。

translations.literal: At that time the hundred officials were utterly swept away; those who survived all hid themselves and would not come out—only Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Shan Wei alone bowed to receive the amnesty below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaucracy had been annihilated; survivors hid and would not appear—only Regular Attendant Shan Wei came alone to the palace gate to receive the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 洛中士民草草，人懷異慮，或雲榮欲縱兵大掠，或雲欲遷都晉陽。

translations.literal: The gentry and common people of Luoyang were in turmoil; each man harbored a different fear—some said Rong wished to let his soldiers plunder on a great scale, others that he meant to move the capital to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang was in uproar; men whispered that Rong would unleash his troops to plunder the city, or that he would move the capital to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 富者棄宅，貧者襁負，率皆逃竄，什不存一二，直衛空虛，官守曠廢。

translations.literal: The rich abandoned their houses, the poor carried their infants on their backs, and all fled; not one or two in ten remained; the palace guard stood empty, offices and posts were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The rich abandoned their houses, the poor fled with infants on their backs; scarcely one household in ten remained; the palace guard stood empty and government offices were deserted.

sentences.zh: 榮乃上書，稱：「大兵交際，難可齊壹，諸王朝貴，橫死者眾，臣今粉軀不足塞咎，乞追贈亡者，微申私責。

translations.literal: Rong then submitted a memorial stating: "When great armies clash, it is hard to keep all in one measure; of the princes and nobles of the court, many were killed wantonly. Your servant's body ground to dust is not enough to answer the blame; I beg posthumous honors for the dead to express a slight private duty.
translations.idiomatic: Rong memorialized: "In the clash of armies discipline breaks down; many princes and nobles died by mischance. My life is not enough to atone; I beg posthumous honors for the dead as a small reparation.

sentences.zh: 無上王請追尊為無上皇帝，自餘死於河陰者，諸王贈三司，三品贈令、僕，五品贈刺史，七品已下及白民贈郡、鎮；

translations.literal: The Prince of Supreme Honor should be posthumously honored as Emperor of Supreme Honor; as for the rest who died at Heyin, princes should be given the Three Excellencies, third rank the posts of Director and Vice Director, fifth rank regional inspectors, seventh rank and below and commoners commanderies and garrisons;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao of Supreme Honor should be posthumously honored as emperor; the rest slain at Heyin—princes as the Three Excellencies, third rank as directors and vice directors, fifth rank as regional inspectors, seventh rank and below and commoners as commandery and garrison posts;

sentences.zh: 死者無後聽繼，即授封爵。

translations.literal: those who died without heirs might have successors appointed, who would at once receive enfeoffment and rank.
translations.idiomatic: the heirless dead might have successors appointed who would immediately receive rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 又遣使者循城勞問。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys to go about the city offering consolation and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys through the city to offer consolation.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " The edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 於是朝士稍出，人心粗安。

translations.literal: Thereupon courtiers gradually came out, and men's hearts were roughly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials gradually emerged, and the city grew somewhat calmer.

sentences.zh: 封無上王之子韶為彭城王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed the Prince of Supreme Honor's son Shao as Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Shao, son of the Prince of Supreme Honor, as Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 榮猶執遷都之議，帝亦不能違。

translations.literal: Rong still clung to the plan to move the capital, and the emperor too could not oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong still pressed to move the capital, and the emperor could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 都官尚書元諶爭之，以為不可，榮怒曰：「何關君事，而固執也！

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Yuan Chen contended with him, saying it could not be done; Rong angrily said: "What business is it of yours that you are so obstinate!
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Clan Yuan Chen argued that it must not be done; Rong snapped, "What is it to you that you are so stubborn?

sentences.zh: 且河陰之役，君應知之。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the affair of Heyin, you ought to know.
translations.idiomatic: You ought to remember Heyin.

sentences.zh: 」諶曰：「天下事當與天下論之，奈何以河陰之酷而恐元諶！

translations.literal: " Chen said: "Affairs of all under Heaven should be debated with all under Heaven—how can you frighten Yuan Chen with the cruelty of Heyin!
translations.idiomatic: " Chen said, "The affairs of the empire must be debated with the empire—do you think the slaughter at Heyin can frighten Yuan Chen?

sentences.zh: 諶，國之宗室，位居常伯，生既無益，死復何損！

translations.literal: Chen is kin of the state, holding the constant rank of chief minister; alive he was of no use, dead of what loss!
translations.idiomatic: I am of the imperial clan and hold high office; alive I have done little good, dead I can do no harm!

sentences.zh: 正使今日碎首流腸，亦無所懼！

translations.literal: Even if today my head is shattered and my bowels pour out, I have nothing to fear!
translations.idiomatic: Even if you dash my brains out today, I do not fear!

sentences.zh: 」榮大怒，欲抵諶罪，爾朱世隆固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: " Rong was greatly angered and wished to punish Chen with a crime; Erzhu Shilong firmly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong was furious and would have punished him, but Erzhu Shilong remonstrated firmly and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 見者莫不震悚，諶顏色自若。

translations.literal: Those who saw it were all shaken with terror; Chen's countenance was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses trembled; Chen's face did not change.

sentences.zh: 後數日，帝與榮登高，見宮闕壯麗，列樹成行，乃歎曰：「臣昨愚闇，有北遷之意，今見皇居之盛，熟思元尚書言，深不可奪。

translations.literal: Several days later the emperor and Rong climbed high, saw the palace halls magnificent and the rows of trees in line, and sighed: "Your servant was foolish and dim yesterday and had the intent to move north; now seeing the splendor of the imperial residence, I have thought over Director Yuan's words carefully—they must not be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the emperor and Rong climbed a height, saw the palace halls in their splendor and trees aligned in rows, and Rong sighed, "I was blind yesterday to think of moving north; seeing the majesty of the capital and weighing Director Yuan's words, that plan cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 」由是罷遷都之議。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the plan to move the capital was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan to move the capital was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 諶，謐之兄也。

translations.literal: Chen was the elder brother of Yuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was the elder brother of Yuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以江陽王繼為太師，北海王顥為太傅；

translations.literal: On day guimao, the Prince of Jiangyang, Ji, was made Grand Preceptor, and the Prince of Beihai, Hao, was made Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Prince Ji of Jiangyang was appointed Grand Preceptor and Prince Hao of Beihai Grand Tutor;

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫李延寔為太保，賜爵濮陽王；

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Li Yanshi was made Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Clan Li Yanshi was made Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang;

sentences.zh: 并州刺史元天穆為太尉，賜爵上黨王；

translations.literal: Bingzhou inspector Yuan Tianmu was made Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Shangdang;
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou inspector Yuan Tianmu was made Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Shangdang;

sentences.zh: 前侍中楊椿為司徒；

translations.literal: former Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Chun was made Minister over the Masses;
translations.idiomatic: former Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Chun was made Minister over the Masses;

sentences.zh: 車騎大將軍穆紹為司空，領尚書令，進爵頓丘王；

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Mu Shao was made Minister of Works, concurrently Director of the Department of State Affairs, and advanced to Prince of Dunqiu;
translations.idiomatic: General of Chariots and Cavalry Mu Shao was made Minister of Works, concurrently Director of the Department of State Affairs, and advanced to Prince of Dunqiu;

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史長孫稚為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，賜爵馮翊王；

translations.literal: Yongzhou inspector Zhangsun Zhi was made General of Agile Cavalry, with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Fengyi;
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou inspector Zhangsun Zhi was made General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Prince of Fengyi;

sentences.zh: 殿中尚書元諶為尚書右僕射，賜爵魏郡王；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yuan Chen was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yuan Chen was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei commandery;

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫廣陵王恭加儀同三司；

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Prince Gong of Guangling was given an office equal to the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Prince Gong of Guangling was given an office equal to the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 其餘起家暴貴者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Of the rest who rose from obscurity to sudden wealth, they could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Countless others who had been obscure men were suddenly raised to high rank.

sentences.zh: 延寔，沖之子也，以帝舅故得超拜。

translations.literal: Yanshi was the son of Chong; because he was the emperor's maternal uncle he received this extraordinary promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi was the son of Li Chong; as the emperor's uncle by marriage he had been promoted far above his station.

sentences.zh: 徐紇弟獻伯為北海太守，季產為青州長史，紇使人告之，皆將家屬逃去，與紇俱奔泰山。

translations.literal: Xu He's younger brother Xianbo was Beihai prefect, and Jichan was Qingzhou chief clerk; He sent men to warn them, and they all fled with their families to join He in fleeing to Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He's younger brother Xianbo was prefect of Beihai and Jichan was chief clerk of Qingzhou; He sent word to them, and they fled with their households to join him on Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 鄭儼與從兄滎陽太守仲明謀據郡起兵，為部下所殺。

translations.literal: Zheng Yan and his elder cousin Zheng Zhongming, prefect of Xingyang, plotted to seize the commandery and raise troops, but were killed by their subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yan and his cousin Zhongming, prefect of Xingyang, plotted to seize the commandery and rebel, but their own officers killed them.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔內外解嚴。

translations.literal: On day dingwei, an edict lifted martial law within and without.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, an edict lifted martial law throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 魏郢州刺史元顯達請降，詔郢州刺史元樹迎之，夏侯夔亦自楚城往會之，遂留鎮焉。

translations.literal: Wei Yingzhou inspector Yuan Xianda requested surrender; an edict ordered Yingzhou inspector Yuan Shu to receive him, and Xia Hou Kui also went from Chucheng to meet him and then remained to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xianda, inspector of Yingzhou in Wei, offered to surrender; the court ordered Yuan Shu, inspector of Yingzhou in Liang, to receive him, and Xia Hou Kui went from Chucheng to join them and remained as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 改魏郢州為北司州，以夔為刺史，兼督司州。

translations.literal: Wei Yingzhou was changed to Northern Sizhou, with Kui as inspector, concurrently supervising Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Yingzhou was redesignated Northern Sizhou, with Kui as inspector and concurrent supervisor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 夔進攻毛城，逼新蔡；

translations.literal: Kui advanced to attack Maocheng and pressed toward Xincai;
translations.idiomatic: Kui advanced against Maocheng and pressed Xincai;

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史夏侯但圍南頓，攻陳項；

translations.literal: Yuzhou inspector Xia Hou Dan besieged Nandun and attacked Chen and Xiang;
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou inspector Xia Hou Dan besieged Nandun and attacked Chen and Xiang;

sentences.zh: 魏行台源子恭拒之。

translations.literal: Wei mobile-staff commander Yuan Zigong resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zigong, commander of the Wei mobile staff, resisted them.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏賜爾朱榮子義羅爵梁郡王。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, Wei enfeoffed Erzhu Rong's son Yiluo as Prince of Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Wei enfeoffed Erzhu Rong's son Yiluo as Prince of Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 柔然頭兵可汗數入貢於魏，魏詔頭兵贊拜不名，上書不稱臣。

translations.literal: The Rouran khan Toubing several times sent tribute to Wei; Wei ordered that when Toubing paid court he need not be named and in memorials he need not style himself subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran khan Toubing sent tribute to Wei several times; Wei decreed that in audience he need not be named and in memorials he need not call himself subject.

sentences.zh: 魏汝南王悅及東道行台臨淮王彧聞河陰之亂，皆來奔。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Runan, Yue, and Eastern-Circuit mobile-staff commander Prince of Huaiyang, Yu, hearing of the Heyin disaster, both came to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue of Runan and Prince Yu of Huaiyang, Eastern-Circuit mobile-staff commander of Wei, hearing of the slaughter at Heyin, both fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏人降者皆稱魏官為偽，彧表啟獨稱魏臨淮王；

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei men who surrendered all called Wei offices false; Yu alone in his memorials styled himself Prince of Huaiyang of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Until then Wei defectors had called Wei offices illegitimate; Yu alone in his memorials styled himself Prince of Huaiyang of Wei;

sentences.zh: 上亦體其雅素，不之責。

translations.literal: the emperor too respected his refined integrity and did not reprove him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor respected his refined integrity and did not reprove him.

sentences.zh: 魏北海王顥將之相州，至汲郡，聞葛榮南侵及爾朱榮縱暴，陰為自安之計，盤桓不進；

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Beihai, Hao, was about to go to Xiangzhou; reaching Ji commandery, he heard that Ge Rong was invading south and that Erzhu Rong was running wild, and secretly formed a plan for his own safety, lingering and not advancing;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hao of Beihai was marching to Xiangzhou; at Ji commandery he heard that Ge Rong was raiding south and Erzhu Rong was running wild, and secretly planned for his own safety, lingering without advancing;

sentences.zh: 以其舅殷州刺史范遵行相州事，代前刺史李神守鄴。

translations.literal: he had his maternal uncle, Yinzhou inspector Fan Zun, act as Xiangzhou affairs while the former inspector Li Shen held Ye.
translations.idiomatic: he left his maternal uncle Fan Zun, inspector of Yinzhou, to manage Xiangzhou while the former inspector Li Shen held Ye.

sentences.zh: 行台甄密知顥有異志，相帥廢遵，復推李神攝州事，遣兵迎顥，且察其變。

translations.literal: Mobile-staff commander Zhen Mi knew Hao harbored a different intent; he and others together deposed Zun, again pushed Li Shen to hold the province, sent troops to meet Hao, and also watched for any change.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile-staff commander Zhen Mi perceived Hao's disloyalty; he and others deposed Zun, restored Li Shen to provisional charge of the province, sent troops to meet Hao, and watched for any move.

sentences.zh: 顥聞之，帥左右來奔。

translations.literal: When Hao heard of it, he led his close attendants and came to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao heard of this he fled with his close attendants.

sentences.zh: 密，琛之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Mi was the son of Zhen Chen's father's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was a cousin of Zhen Chen.

sentences.zh: 北青州刺史元世俊、南荊州刺史李志皆舉州來降。

translations.literal: Northern Qingzhou inspector Yuan Shijun and Southern Jingzhou inspector Li Zhi both raised their provinces and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shijun, inspector of Northern Qingzhou, and Li Zhi, inspector of Southern Jingzhou, both surrendered their provinces to Liang.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁巳朔，魏加爾朱榮北道大行台。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day dingsi of the month, Wei added Erzhu Rong as Northern-Circuit Grand Mobile-Staff Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the month's dingsi new moon, Wei added Erzhu Rong as Northern-Circuit Grand Mobile-Staff Commander.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右僕射元羅為東道大使，光祿勳元欣副之，巡方黜陟，先行後聞。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Yuan Luo was made Eastern-Circuit commissioner, with Director of the Imperial Clan Yuan Xin as his deputy, to tour the regions for promotion and demotion, acting first and reporting afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Yuan Luo was made Eastern-Circuit commissioner, with Director of the Imperial Clan Yuan Xin as deputy, to tour the regions for promotions and demotions, acting first and reporting afterward.

sentences.zh: 欣，羽之子也。

translations.literal: Xin was the son of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was the son of Yuan Yu.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮入見魏主於明光殿，重謝河橋之事，誓言無復貳心。
