translations.literal: Erzhu Rong entered to see the Wei sovereign at Bright Light Hall, again apologized for the affair at Heyin, and swore he would never again harbor a second heart.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong entered to see the Wei emperor at Bright Light Hall, apologized again for Heyin, and swore he would never again waver in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 帝自起止之，因復為榮誓，言無疑心。

translations.literal: The emperor himself rose to stop him and in turn swore to Rong that he had no suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose to restrain him and in turn swore he harbored no suspicion.

sentences.zh: 榮喜，因求酒飲之，熟醉；

translations.literal: Rong was pleased, and therefore asked for wine and drank; he became thoroughly drunk;
translations.idiomatic: Rong was pleased, asked for wine, and drank himself into a stupor;

sentences.zh: 帝欲誅之，左右苦諫，乃止，即以床輿向中常侍省。

translations.literal: the emperor wished to execute him, but those at his side remonstrated bitterly and he stopped, and had him carried on a couch to the Directorate of Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor wished to kill him, but attendants remonstrated bitterly and he desisted, and had Rong carried on a couch to the eunuchs' quarters.

sentences.zh: 榮夜半方寤，遂達旦不眠，自此不復禁中宿矣。

translations.literal: Rong only came to at midnight; from then on he did not sleep within the palace, and from this time he no longer lodged inside the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Rong did not wake until midnight; from then on he never again lodged within the palace.

sentences.zh: 榮女先為肅宗嬪，榮欲敬宗立以為後，帝疑未決，給事黃門侍郎祖瑩曰：「昔文公在秦，懷嬴入侍；

translations.literal: Rong's daughter had earlier been a consort of Emperor Suzong; Rong wished to have Emperor Jingzong enthroned and make her empress; the emperor hesitated and had not decided; Attendant of Scattered Retinues Zu Ying said: "Long ago Duke Wen of Jin was in Qin and Huai Ying entered to serve;
translations.idiomatic: Rong's daughter had been a consort of Emperor Xiaoming; Rong wished Emperor Jingzong enthroned and to make her empress; the emperor hesitated; Attendant Zu Ying said, "Long ago Duke Wen of Jin was in Qin and Huai Ying entered to serve him;

sentences.zh: 事有反經合義，陛下獨何疑焉！

translations.literal: affairs may run counter to the norm yet accord with righteousness—why should Your Majesty alone hesitate!
translations.idiomatic: there are times when affairs run counter to the norm yet accord with righteousness—why should Your Majesty alone hesitate?

sentences.zh: 」帝遂從之，榮意甚悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon followed this, and Rong was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed this, and Rong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 榮舉止輕脫，喜馳射，每入朝見，更無所為，唯戲上下馬；

translations.literal: Rong's conduct was frivolous and unceremonious; he delighted in galloping and shooting; each time he came to court he did nothing else but play at mounting and dismounting;
translations.idiomatic: Rong's conduct was frivolous; he loved galloping and archery; at each court audience he did nothing but play at mounting and dismounting;

sentences.zh: 於西林園宴射，恆請皇后出觀，並召王公、妃主共在一堂。

translations.literal: at banquets for shooting in the Western Grove Garden he always asked the empress to come out and watch, and also summoned princes, dukes, consorts, and princesses to sit together in one hall.
translations.idiomatic: at shooting banquets in the Western Grove Garden he always asked the empress to come out and watch, and summoned princes, dukes, consorts, and princesses to sit together in one hall.

sentences.zh: 每見天子射中，輒自起舞叫，將相卿士悉皆盤旋，乃至妃主亦不免隨之舉袂。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw the Son of Heaven hit the target, he himself would rise and dance and shout; generals, ministers, and scholars all whirled about, and even consorts and princesses could not avoid lifting their sleeves and joining in.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor hit the target, he would leap up dancing and shouting; generals, ministers, and scholars all whirled about, and even consorts and princesses lifted their sleeves and joined in.

sentences.zh: 及酒酣耳熱，必自匡坐唱虜歌；

translations.literal: When wine had warmed his ears, he would always rise from his seat and sing barbarian songs;
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had warmed him, he would rise from his seat and sing barbarian songs;

sentences.zh: 日暮罷歸，與左右連手蹋地唱《回波樂》而出。

translations.literal: at dusk he would leave, and with his attendants join hands, stamp the ground, and sing "Waves Returning" as they went out.
translations.idiomatic: at dusk he would leave, join hands with his attendants, stamp the ground, and sing "Waves Returning" as they went out.

sentences.zh: 性甚嚴暴，喜慍無恆，刀槊弓矢，不離於手，每有瞋嫌，即行擊射，左右恆有死憂。

translations.literal: By nature he was very stern and violent; joy and anger had no constancy; blades, spears, bows, and arrows never left his hand; whenever he felt anger he would strike or shoot at once, and those at his side constantly faced the fear of death.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was savage and violent, his moods without constancy; blades, spears, bows, and arrows never left his hand; at the least resentment he would strike or shoot, and those around him lived in constant fear of death.

sentences.zh: 嘗見沙彌重騎一馬，榮即令相觸，力窮不復能動，遂使旁人以頭相擊，死而後已。

translations.literal: Once he saw a shramana heavily riding one horse; Rong at once ordered them to charge each other; when their strength was exhausted and they could no longer move, he had those beside them strike head against head until they died, and only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once he saw a monk heavily mounted on one horse; Rong ordered them to charge each other; when both were exhausted and could not move, he had bystanders butt their heads together until they died, and only then stopped.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，榮還晉陽，帝餞之於邙陰。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, Rong returned to Jinyang; the emperor saw him off at the northern slope of Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Rong returned to Jinyang; the emperor saw him off on the northern slope of Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 榮令元天穆入洛陽，加天穆侍中、錄尚書事、京畿大都督兼領軍將軍，以行台郎中桑干朱瑞為黃門侍郎兼中書舍人，朝廷要官，悉用其腹心為之。

translations.literal: Rong ordered Yuan Tianmu to enter Luoyang, added Tianmu as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Recorder of the Department of State Affairs, Metropolitan Commander of the Capital District, and concurrently General of the Palace Garrison, appointed mobile-staff gentleman Sanggan Zhu Rui as Attendant of Scattered Retinues and concurrently Secretariat Drafter; important offices of the court were all filled with men in whom he placed his trust.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent Yuan Tianmu into Luoyang, made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Recorder of the Department of State Affairs, Metropolitan Commander of the Capital District, and concurrently General of the Palace Garrison, and appointed mobile-staff gentleman Zhu Rui of Sanggan as Attendant of Scattered Retinues and concurrently Secretariat drafter; every important post at court was filled with his own men.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，魏主詔：「孝昌以來，凡有冤抑無訴者，悉集華林東門，當親理之。

translations.literal: On day bingyin, the Wei sovereign issued an edict: "Since the Xiaochang era, all who have suffered injustice without redress shall assemble at the east gate of Hualin, and I shall judge them in person.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the Wei emperor issued an edict: "Since the Xiaochang era, all who have suffered injustice without redress shall assemble at the east gate of Hualin, and I shall judge them in person.

sentences.zh: 」時承喪亂之後，倉廩虛竭，始詔「入粟八千石者賜爵散侯，白民輸五百石者賜出身，沙門授本州統及郡縣維那。

translations.literal: " At that time, after the succession of bereavements and disorder, the granaries were empty; an edict was first issued that "those who contribute eight thousand piculs of grain shall be enfeoffed as Marquis Who Spreads Goodness, commoners who contribute five hundred piculs shall receive the first rank of office, and Buddhist monks shall be granted headship of their native province and of commandery and county Buddhist associations.
translations.idiomatic: " In the wake of rebellion the granaries stood empty; the court first decreed that contributors of eight thousand piculs of grain should be enfeoffed as Marquis Who Spreads Goodness, commoners who gave five hundred piculs should receive the first rank of office, and monks should be granted headship of their native province and of commandery and county Buddhist associations.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮之趣洛也，遣其都督樊子鵠取唐州，唐州刺史崔元珍、行台酈惲拒守不從。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong pressed toward Luoyang, he sent his commander Fan Zihu to take Tangzhou; Tangzhou inspector Cui Yuanzhen and mobile-staff commander Li Yun defended and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang he sent his commander Fan Zihu to take Tangzhou; Inspector Cui Yuanzhen and mobile-staff commander Li Yun defended the city and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，子鵠拔平陽，斬元珍及惲。

translations.literal: On day yihai, Zihu captured Pingyang and beheaded Yuanzhen and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Zihu captured Pingyang and beheaded Yuanzhen and Yun.

sentences.zh: 元珍，挺之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen was the son of his father's younger brother to Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen was a cousin of Cui Ting.

sentences.zh: 將軍曹義宗圍魏荊州，堰水灌城，不沒者數板。

translations.literal: General Cao Yizong besieged Wei Jingzhou, dammed the waters to flood the city, and only a few courses of wall remained above the water.
translations.idiomatic: General Cao Yizong besieged Jingzhou in Wei, dammed the waters to flood the city, and only a few courses of wall stood above the flood.

sentences.zh: 時魏方多難，不能救，城中糧盡，刺史王羆煮粥，與將士均分食之。

translations.literal: At that time Wei was beset by many troubles and could not rescue it; grain in the city was exhausted, and inspector Wang Pi cooked gruel and shared it equally with his officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was beset by troubles and could not relieve the city; when grain ran out, Inspector Wang Pi cooked gruel and shared it equally with his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 每出戰，不擐甲冑，仰天大呼曰：「荊州城，孝文皇帝所置，天若不祐國家，令箭中王羆額；

translations.literal: Each time he went out to battle he did not don armor or helmet, but looked up to Heaven and shouted loudly: "Jingzhou city was established by Emperor Xiaowen; if Heaven does not protect the state, let the arrow strike Wang Pi in the forehead;
translations.idiomatic: Each time he fought he wore no armor or helmet, but shouted to Heaven: "Jingzhou was founded by Emperor Xiaowen; if Heaven will not protect the dynasty, let the arrow strike Wang Pi in the brow;

sentences.zh: 不爾，王羆必當破賊！

translations.literal: if not, Wang Pi will surely break the bandits!
translations.idiomatic: if not, Wang Pi will surely break the enemy!

sentences.zh: 」彌歷三年，前後搏戰甚眾，亦不被傷。

translations.literal: " For three years they fought back and forth in very many battles, yet he was never wounded.
translations.idiomatic: " For three years they fought battle after battle, yet he was never wounded.

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏以中軍將軍費穆都督南征諸軍事，將兵救之。

translations.literal: On day guiwei, Wei appointed Central Army general Fei Mu commander of the southern campaign and sent troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Wei appointed Central Army general Fei Mu commander of the southern campaign and sent troops to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 魏臨淮王彧聞魏主定位，乃以母老求還，辭情懇至。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Huaiyang, Yu, hearing that the Wei sovereign had taken the throne, then because his mother was old asked to return; his words were earnest to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu of Huaiyang, hearing that the Wei emperor had been enthroned, begged to return because his mother was old; his plea was most earnest.

sentences.zh: 上惜其才而不能違，六月，丁亥，遣彧還。

translations.literal: The emperor prized his talent and could not refuse; in the sixth month, on day dinghai, he sent Yu back.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor prized his talent and could not refuse; in the sixth month, on dinghai, he sent Yu back.

sentences.zh: 魏以彧為侍中、驃騎大將軍，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wei made Yu Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Agile Cavalry and gave him an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Yu Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Agile Cavalry and gave him an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 魏員外散騎常侍高乾，祐之從子也，與弟敖曹、季式皆喜輕俠，與魏主有舊。

translations.literal: Wei Supernumerary Palace Attendant Gao Gan was the son of You's younger brother; with his younger brothers Aocao and Jishi he all delighted in dashing gallantry and had old ties with the Wei sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Wei supernumerary Palace Attendant Gao Gan was a nephew of Gao You; he and his younger brothers Aocao and Jishi all loved reckless gallantry and had old ties with the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮之向洛也，逃奔齊州，聞河陰之亂，遂集流民起兵於河、濟之間，受葛榮官爵，頻破州軍。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong marched toward Luoyang, he fled to Qizhou; hearing of the Heyin disaster, he gathered displaced people and raised troops between the Yellow River and Ji River, accepted office and rank from Ge Rong, and repeatedly defeated provincial armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang he fled to Qizhou; hearing of Heyin he gathered refugees and raised troops between the Yellow River and the Ji, accepted rank from Ge Rong, and repeatedly defeated provincial armies.

sentences.zh: 魏主使元欣諭旨，乾等乃降。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign sent Yuan Xin to announce the imperial will, and Gan and the others thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent Yuan Xin with the imperial message, and Gan and his brothers surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以乾為給事黃門侍郎兼武衛將軍，敖曹為通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Gan was made Attendant of Scattered Retinues and concurrently Martial Guard general, and Aocao was made Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was made Attendant of Scattered Retinues and concurrently Martial Guard general, and Aocao Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 榮以乾兄弟前為叛亂，不應復居近要，魏主乃聽解官歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Rong, because the Gao brothers had earlier joined rebellion, said they ought not again to hold posts close to the throne; the Wei sovereign then permitted them to resign office and return to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: Rong argued that the Gao brothers, having rebelled before, should not again hold posts near the throne; the Wei emperor let them resign and return home.

sentences.zh: 敖曹復行抄掠，榮誘執之，與薛修義同拘於晉陽。

translations.literal: Aocao again went raiding; Rong lured him in and seized him, and detained him at Jinyang together with Xue Xiuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Aocao took to raiding again; Rong lured him in and seized him, and held him at Jinyang together with Xue Xiuyi.

sentences.zh: 敖曹名昂，以字行。

translations.literal: Aocao's name was Ang; he was known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Aocao's given name was Ang; he was known by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 葛榮軍乏食，遣其僕射任褒將軍南掠至沁水。

translations.literal: Ge Rong's army lacked food; he sent his Vice Director Ren Bao, commanding troops, south to plunder as far as Qinshui.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong's army lacked food; he sent his vice director Ren Bao south to plunder as far as Qinshui.

sentences.zh: 魏以元天穆為大都督東北道諸軍事，帥宗正珍孫等討之。

translations.literal: Wei made Yuan Tianmu Grand Commander of Northeastern-Circuit military affairs and led Director of the Imperial Clan Zhen Sun and others to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Yuan Tianmu grand commander of Northeastern-Circuit military affairs and sent Director of the Imperial Clan Zhen Sun and others against him.

sentences.zh: 前幽州平北府主簿河間邢杲帥河北流民十萬餘戶反於青州之北海，自稱漢王，改元天統。

translations.literal: Former chief clerk of the Pingbei office in Youzhou, Xing Shuo of Hejian, led more than one hundred thousand households of displaced people north of the Yellow River in rebellion at Beihai in Qingzhou, styled himself King of Han, and changed the era name to Tiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shuo of Hejian, former chief clerk of the Pingbei office in Youzhou, led more than a hundred thousand refugee households in revolt at Beihai in Qingzhou, styled himself King of Han, and changed the era name to Tiantong.

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏以征東將軍李叔仁為車騎大將軍、儀同三司，帥眾討之。

translations.literal: On day wushen, Wei made Eastern Campaign general Li Shuren General of Chariots and Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies and led the host to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Wei made Eastern Campaign general Li Shuren General of Chariots and Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies and sent him against Xing Shuo.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏主詔曰：「朕當親御六戎，掃靜燕、代。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, the Wei sovereign issued an edict stating: "I shall personally lead the six armies and pacify Yan and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Wei emperor issued an edict: "I shall personally lead the six armies and pacify Yan and Dai.

sentences.zh: 」以大將軍爾朱榮為左軍，上黨王穆為前國，司徒楊椿為右軍，司空穆紹為後軍。

translations.literal: " He made Grand General Erzhu Rong the left army, Prince of Shangdang Mu the vanguard, Minister over the Masses Yang Chun the right army, and Minister of Works Mu Shao the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: " He made Grand General Erzhu Rong the left wing, Prince of Shangdang Mu the vanguard, Minister over the Masses Yang Chun the right wing, and Minister of Works Mu Shao the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 葛榮退屯相州之北。

translations.literal: Ge Rong withdrew and encamped north of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong withdrew and encamped north of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙丑，魏加爾朱榮柱國大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on day yichou, Wei added Erzhu Rong as Pillar of State, Grand General, and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on yichou, Wei added Erzhu Rong as Pillar of State, Grand General, and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 壬子，魏光州民劉舉聚眾反於濮陽，自稱皇武大將軍。

translations.literal: On day renzi, the people of Guang province in Wei, Liu Ju, gathered a host in rebellion at Puyang and styled himself Grand General of August Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the people of Guang province in Wei, Liu Ju, rose at Puyang and styled himself Grand General of August Martiality.

sentences.zh: 是月，-{万俟}-丑奴自稱天子，置百官。

translations.literal: That month, Wanqi Chounu styled himself Son of Heaven and established the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Wanqi Chounu styled himself Son of Heaven and established the full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 會波斯國獻師子於魏，丑奴留之，改元神獸。

translations.literal: It happened that the state of Persia presented a lion to Wei; Chounu kept it and changed the era name to Divine Beast.
translations.idiomatic: Persia had just presented a lion to Wei; Chounu kept the gift and changed his era name to Divine Beast.

sentences.zh: 魏泰山太守羊侃，以其祖規嘗為宋高祖祭酒從事，常有南歸之志。

translations.literal: Wei Taishan prefect Yang Kan, because his grandfather Gui had once been a follower of attendants for libation under Song Emperor Gaozu, constantly harbored the will to return south.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan, prefect of Taishan in Wei, whose grandfather Gui had once served as libationer under Emperor Wu of Song, long harbored the wish to return south.

sentences.zh: 徐紇往依之，因勸侃起兵，侃從之。

translations.literal: Xu He went to rely on him and therefore urged Kan to raise troops; Kan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He came to him for refuge and urged him to rebel; Kan agreed.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史羊敦，侃之從兄也，密知之，據州拒侃。

translations.literal: Yanzhou inspector Yang Dun, Kan's elder cousin, secretly learned of it and held the province to resist Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou inspector Yang Dun, Kan's cousin, learned of the plot in secret and held the province against him.

sentences.zh: 八月，侃引兵襲敦，弗克，築十餘城守之，且遣使來降；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Kan led troops to strike Dun but could not overcome him; he built more than ten fortified camps to hold his ground and also sent envoys to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Kan attacked Dun but could not take him; he built more than ten fortified camps and sent envoys to surrender to Liang;

sentences.zh: 詔廣晉縣侯泰山羊鴉仁等將兵應接。

translations.literal: an edict ordered Marquis of Guangjin county Yang Yaren and others to lead troops to meet and support him.
translations.idiomatic: the court ordered Marquis Yaren of Guangjin and others to lead troops to his aid.

sentences.zh: 魏以侃為驃騎大將軍、泰山公、兗州刺史，侃斬其使者不受。

translations.literal: Wei made Kan General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Taishan, and Yanzhou inspector; Kan beheaded the envoys and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Kan General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Taishan, and inspector of Yanzhou; Kan beheaded their envoys and refused.

sentences.zh: 將軍王弁侵魏徐州，蕃郡民續靈珍擁眾萬人攻蕃城以應梁；

translations.literal: General Wang Bian invaded Wei Xuzhou; the people of Fan commandery, Xu Lingzhen, gathered a host of ten thousand men and attacked Fancheng in support of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Bian invaded Xuzhou in Wei; Xu Lingzhen of Fan commandery gathered ten thousand men and attacked Fancheng in support of Liang;

sentences.zh: 魏徐州刺史楊昱擊靈珍，斬之，弁引還。

translations.literal: Wei Xuzhou inspector Yang Yu attacked Lingzhen, beheaded him, and Bian withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu, inspector of Xuzhou in Wei, attacked Lingzhen, beheaded him, and Bian withdrew.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏大都督宗正珍孫擊舉於濮陽，滅之。

translations.literal: On day jiachen, Wei Grand Commander Zhen Sun attacked Ju at Puyang and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Wei Grand Commander Zhen Sun attacked Liu Ju at Puyang and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 葛榮引兵圍鄴，眾號百萬，遊兵已過汲郡，所至殘掠，爾朱榮啟求討之。

translations.literal: Ge Rong led troops to besiege Ye; his host was said to number a million; roaming soldiers had already passed Ji commandery; wherever they went they ravaged and plundered; Erzhu Rong memorialized requesting to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong led his army to besiege Ye; his force was said to number a million; raiding parties had already passed Ji commandery, ravaging wherever they went; Erzhu Rong memorialized asking leave to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 九月，爾朱榮召從子肆州刺史天光留鎮晉陽，曰：「我身不得至處，非汝無以稱我心。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Erzhu Rong summoned his nephew, Sizhou inspector Tianguang, to remain and garrison Jinyang, saying: "Where I myself cannot go, none but you can satisfy my heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Erzhu Rong summoned his nephew Tianguang, inspector of Sizhou, to garrison Jinyang, saying, "Where I cannot go in person, none but you can do what I wish.

sentences.zh: 」自帥精騎七千，馬皆有副，倍道兼行。

translations.literal: " He himself led seven thousand picked horsemen, each horse with a spare mount, and marched day and night.
translations.idiomatic: " He himself led seven thousand picked horsemen, each with a spare mount, and marched day and night.

sentences.zh: 東出滏口，以侯景為前驅。

translations.literal: He went east out of Fukou, with Hou Jing as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He marched east out of Fukou with Hou Jing as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 葛榮為盜日久，橫行河北，爾朱榮眾寡非敵，議者謂無取勝之理。

translations.literal: Ge Rong had long been a bandit, ranging freely through Hebei; Erzhu Rong's numbers could not match the enemy; debaters said there was no principle by which he could win.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong had long been a bandit lord across Hebei; Erzhu Rong was vastly outnumbered; court opinion held he could not win.

sentences.zh: 葛榮聞之，喜見於色，令其眾曰：「此易與耳，諸人俱辦長繩，至則縛取。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong heard of it, joy showed in his face; he ordered his host: "This will be easy; all of you prepare long ropes—when they arrive, bind and take them.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong heard this, joy showed on his face; he told his men, "This will be easy—everyone prepare long ropes; when they come, bind them and take them.

sentences.zh: 」自鄴以北，列陳數十里，箕張而進。

translations.literal: " From Ye northward they drew up battle lines for several tens of li, spreading out like a winnowing basket as they advanced.
translations.idiomatic: " From Ye northward they drew up battle lines for tens of li, fanning out as they advanced.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮潛軍山谷，為奇兵，分督將已上三人為一處，處有數百騎，令所在揚塵鼓噪，使賊不測多少。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong hid his army in a valley as a surprise force; he divided supervising generals and above, three to a place, each place with several hundred horsemen, and ordered that wherever they were they should raise dust and clamor so the bandits could not gauge their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong hid troops in a valley as a surprise force; he grouped supervising generals and above in threes, several hundred horsemen to each group, and ordered them to raise dust and clamor everywhere so the rebels could not tell how many he had.

sentences.zh: 又以人馬逼戰，刀不如棒，勒軍士繼袖棒一枚，置於馬側，至戰時慮廢騰逐，不聽斬級，以棒棒之而已。

translations.literal: Also, when men and horses fought at close quarters, blades were not as good as clubs; he ordered the soldiers each to tie one club to his sleeve and place it at the horse's side; at battle he feared that pursuit and cutting off heads would waste the charge, and he did not permit taking heads—only to club them.
translations.idiomatic: In close fighting, he held, blades were inferior to clubs; he ordered every soldier to tie a club to his sleeve and keep it at his saddle; at the clash he feared pursuit and head-taking would break the charge, and forbade decapitation—only clubbing.

sentences.zh: 分命壯勇所向衝突，號令嚴明，戰士同奮。

translations.literal: He assigned the brave to charge wherever directed; orders were strict and clear; the warriors fought with one accord.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his strongest men charging wherever the line gave way; discipline was iron; every soldier fought as one.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮身自陷陳，出於賊後，表裡合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong himself entered the battle formation, emerged behind the bandits, and struck from within and without; he utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong charged in person, circled behind the enemy, and struck from both sides; the rebel host was shattered.

sentences.zh: 於陳擒葛榮，餘眾悉降。

translations.literal: On the battlefield he captured Ge Rong; the remaining host all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Ge Rong on the field; the rest surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 以賊徒既眾，若即分割，恐其疑懼，或更結聚，乃下令各從所樂，親屬相隨，任所居止。

translations.literal: Because the bandit followers were so numerous, if he divided them at once he feared they would grow suspicious and alarmed, or gather again; he therefore ordered that each might follow his own pleasure, kin go with kin, and settle wherever they wished.
translations.idiomatic: The captives were so numerous that immediate dispersal might alarm them into regrouping; he therefore decreed that each man might go where he pleased, kin with kin, and settle as he chose.

sentences.zh: 於是群情大喜，登即四散，數十萬眾一朝散盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the host was greatly pleased, and at once scattered in all directions; several hundred thousand men dispersed in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: The captives were overjoyed and at once scattered; several hundred thousand melted away in one morning.

sentences.zh: 待出百里之外，乃始分道押領，隨便安置，鹹得其宜。

translations.literal: After they had gone beyond a hundred li, he then began to escort them by separate routes and settle them as convenient; all found suitable placement.
translations.idiomatic: Only after they had gone a hundred li did he escort them by detachments and resettle them; every man found a fitting place.

sentences.zh: 擢其渠帥，量才授任，新附者鹹安，時人服其處分機速。

translations.literal: He promoted their chieftains and assigned posts according to talent; the newly submitted were all at ease; contemporaries admired his swift and decisive handling.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted rebel leaders and gave each office suited to his gifts; the new subjects were pacified; men marveled at how swiftly he had settled the matter.

sentences.zh: 以檻車送葛榮赴洛，冀、定、滄、瀛、殷五州皆平。

translations.literal: In a caged cart he sent Ge Rong to Luoyang; the five provinces Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, and Yin were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong was sent to Luoyang in a prisoner cart; Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, and Yin were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 時上黨王天穆軍於朝歌之南，穆紹、楊椿猶未發，而葛榮已滅，乃皆罷兵。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Tianmu of Shangdang had his army south of Chaoge; Mu Shao and Yang Chun had not yet marched, but Ge Rong was already destroyed, and all therefore demobilized.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tianmu of Shangdang was encamped south of Chaoge; Mu Shao and Yang Chun had not yet set out—but Ge Rong was already destroyed, and all stood down.

sentences.zh: 初，宇文肱從鮮于修禮攻定州，戰死於唐河。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuwen Gong followed Xianyu Xiuli in attacking Dingzhou and died in battle on the Tang River.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuwen Gong had followed Xianyu Xiuli against Dingzhou and was killed on the Tang River.

sentences.zh: 其子泰在修禮軍中，修禮死，從葛榮；

translations.literal: His son Tai was in Xiuli's army; when Xiuli died he followed Ge Rong;
translations.idiomatic: His son Tai served in Xiuli's army; when Xiuli fell he joined Ge Rong;

sentences.zh: 葛榮敗，爾朱榮愛泰之才，以為統軍。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong was defeated, Erzhu Rong admired Tai's talent and made him commandant of an army.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong's defeat Erzhu Rong prized Tai's ability and made him army commandant.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏大赦，改元永遠。

translations.literal: On yihai, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Wei proclaimed a grand amnesty and adopted the era name Yongyuan.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以爾朱榮為大丞相、都督河北畿外諸軍事，榮子平昌公文殊、昌樂公文暢並進爵為王，以楊椿為太保，城陽王徽為司徒。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Erzhu Rong was made Grand Chancellor and commander-in-chief of all military affairs in and beyond the Hebei belt; Rong's sons Wenqu, Duke of Pingchang, and Wenchang, Duke of Changle, were both advanced to princely rank; Yang Chun was made Grand Guardian and Prince Hui of Chengyang Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Erzhu Rong was made Grand Chancellor and commander of all forces in and beyond the Hebei belt; his sons Wenqu of Pingchang and Wenchang of Changle were both advanced to princely rank; Yang Chun was made Grand Guardian and Prince Hui of Chengyang Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁亥，葛榮至洛，魏主御閶闔門引見，斬於都市。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dinghai, Ge Rong reached Luoyang; the Wei sovereign received him at the Chongye Gate and executed him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on dinghai, Ge Rong reached Luoyang; the Wei emperor received him at the Chongye Gate and had him beheaded in the market.

sentences.zh: 帝以魏北海王顥為魏王，遣東宮直閤將軍陳慶之將兵送之還北。

translations.literal: The emperor made Prince Hao of Beihai in Wei into Prince of Wei and sent Eastern Palace Attendant-General Chen Qingzhi with troops to escort him back north.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor named Prince Hao of Beihai the Prince of Wei and sent Chen Qingzhi of the Eastern Palace guard with an army to escort him north.

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏以太原王世子爾朱菩提為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司；

translations.literal: On bingshen, Wei made Erzhu Puti, heir of the Prince of Taiyuan, General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Wei made Puti, heir of the Prince of Taiyuan, General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以長樂等七郡各萬戶，通前十萬戶，為太原王榮國；

translations.literal: On dingyou, seven commanderies including Changle, ten thousand households each—for one hundred thousand households in all—were made the fief of Prince Rong of Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, seven commanderies including Changle were granted ten thousand households apiece—one hundred thousand households in all—as the fief of Prince Rong of Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 戊戌，又加榮太師；

translations.literal: On wuxu, Rong was further given the title Grand Preceptor;
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Rong was further made Grand Preceptor;

sentences.zh: 皆賞擒葛榮之功也。

translations.literal: All this was to reward the merit of capturing Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: All were rewards for capturing Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 壬子，魏江陽武烈王繼卒。

translations.literal: On renzi, Prince Ji of Jiangyang, styled Wulie, died in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Prince Ji of Jiangyang, posthumous name Wulie, died.

sentences.zh: 魏使征虜將軍韓子熙招諭邢杲，杲詐降而復反。

translations.literal: Wei sent Campaigning General Han Zixi to summon and instruct Xing Gao; Gao feigned surrender and rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Campaigning General Han Zixi to parley with Xing Gao; Gao feigned submission and rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 李叔仁擊杲於濰水，失利而還。

translations.literal: Li Shuren attacked Gao at the Wei River, was defeated, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuren attacked Gao on the Wei River, was beaten, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 魏費穆奄至荊州，曹義宗軍敗，為魏所擒，荊州之圍始解。

translations.literal: Wei Fei Mu suddenly reached Jingzhou; Cao Yizong's army was defeated and he was captured by Wei; the siege of Jingzhou was at last lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu of Wei suddenly appeared at Jingzhou; Cao Yizong was defeated and taken; the siege of Jingzhou was finally raised.

sentences.zh: 元顥取魏銍城而據之。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao took Wei's Cheng city and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao seized the city of Cheng in Wei and held it.

sentences.zh: 魏行台尚書左僕射於暉等兵數十萬，擊羊侃於瑕丘，徐紇恐事不濟，說侃請乞師於梁，侃信之，紇遂來奔。

translations.literal: Wei mobile-staff Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Yu Hui and others with an army of several hundred thousand attacked Yang Kan at Xiqiu; Xu He feared affairs would not succeed, persuaded Kan to beg Liang for reinforcements; Kan believed him, and He thereupon came to defect.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hui, Left Vice Director on the Wei mobile staff, led several hundred thousand men against Yang Kan at Xiqiu; Xu He, fearing defeat, urged Kan to ask Liang for help; Kan believed him and He fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 暉等圍侃十餘重，機中矢盡，南軍不進。

translations.literal: Hui and the others besieged Kan in more than ten lines; crossbows and machines ran out of arrows; the southern army did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's host pinned Kan in more than ten rings of siege; bolts and machines ran dry; the southern relief force never came.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸亥夜，侃潰圍出，且戰且行，一日一夜乃出魏境，至渣口，眾尚萬餘人，馬二千匹。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the night of guihai, Kan broke through the encirclement; fighting as he went, in one day and one night he left Wei territory and reached Zhakou; his host still numbered more than ten thousand men and two thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of guihai in the eleventh month Kan broke the siege; fighting all the way, he crossed out of Wei in a day and a night and reached Zhakou with more than ten thousand men and two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 士卒皆竟夜悲歌，侃乃謝曰：「卿等懷土，理不能見隨，幸適去留，於此為別。

translations.literal: The soldiers all sang mournfully through the night; Kan then apologized, saying: "You long for home—it is only right that I cannot ask you all to follow; I wish you may go or stay as you please—here we part."
translations.idiomatic: His men sang laments through the night; Kan bowed to them and said, "You pine for home—I cannot ask you all to follow; go or stay as you will—here we take leave."

sentences.zh: 」各拜辭而去。

translations.literal: " Each bowed farewell and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Each man bowed and went his way.

sentences.zh: 魏復取泰山。

translations.literal: Wei recovered Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei recovered Mount Tai commandery.

sentences.zh: 暉，勁之子也。

translations.literal: Hui was the son of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was the son of Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，魏以上黨王天穆為大將軍、開府儀同三司，世襲并州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Wei made Prince Tianmu of Shangdang Grand General with an office equal to the Three Excellencies and hereditary Bingzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Wei made Prince Tianmu of Shangdang Grand General with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, with hereditary rank as Bingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚子，魏詔於暉還師討邢杲。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, Wei ordered Yu Hui to return his army and campaign against Xing Gao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, Wei ordered Yu Hui to withdraw and campaign against Xing Gao.

sentences.zh: 葛榮餘黨韓樓復據幽州反，北邊被其患。

translations.literal: Ge Rong's remnant follower Han Lou again seized Youzhou and rebelled; the northern border suffered from his raids.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lou, a remnant of Ge Rong's host, seized Youzhou again and rebelled; the northern marches groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮以撫軍將軍賀拔勝為大都督，鎮中山；

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong made Pacification Army general Heba Sheng supreme commander and garrisoned him at Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong appointed Pacification Army general Heba Sheng supreme commander and posted him at Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 樓畏勝威名，不敢南出。

translations.literal: Lou feared Sheng's renown and dared not march south.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lou feared Sheng's name and dared not march south.
